A new report has proposed a £1-per-night tourist tax for travellers to York and North Yorkshire.

The Visitor Levy Policy Report commissioned by the mayor of York and North Yorkshire, David Skaith, was published on Monday.

It said a flat visitor levy could raise between £26m and £52m annually for the region to “invest back into its hospitality and tourism industry”.

The area welcomed 7.8 million overnight visitors in 2024.

According to the report, the fee would be paid via a digital platform, with possible exemptions for low-cost stays including campsites.

Visitor growth in destinations such as Edinburgh, Paris and Barcelona since introducing a fee was used as evidence that a modest levy will not deter visitors.

Skaith said: “York and North Yorkshire has something for everyone. Millions visit every year, and that’s why a visitor levy could be a total game changer for us.

"Thriving communities and thriving destinations go hand in hand, but welcoming so many visitors puts pressure on the infrastructure and services our residents rely on.

"We must get this right for our county so we can invest in our communities, and our hospitality and tourism businesses. That's why I'm committed to keep talking with the sector as the details come together."

The national legislative framework enabling English mayors to introduce visitor levies is progressing through Parliament, with the English Devolution and Community Empowerment Bill currently in the House of Lords.

The earliest implementation date will likely be in 2027 or 2028.

Professor Brendan Paddison, Dean of York Business School said: “Good policy starts with good evidence. This report is not about making the case for or against a visitor levy; it is about giving the Mayor, businesses and communities the evidence they need to have an informed conversation about what could work for York and North Yorkshire.”

Milder conditions are set to return following a rainy start to the week as temperatures are forecast to creep back up to 24C.

Heavy rain is set to sweep across the UK on Tuesday with temperatures plunging to 11C in Scotland and 15C in the south of England.

Although the weather has changed bringing more unsettled conditions, all of Wales and most of England remains in drought. That’s because sustained rainfall is needed to reverse the drought conditions.

In the south of England Tuesday will be the wettest day of the week, but in the north of England Manchester is set to see showers from Thursday afternoon.

open image in gallery Most of the UK is set to see heavy rain on Tuesday before warmer conditions return ( Met Office )

By Saturday temperatures in London will reach 23C, with highs of 19C in Cardiff and 17C in Manchester. On Monday the capital will see highs of 24C and most of England and Wales will see temperatures in the low 20C in a warm start to the week.

It comes after the Met Office this week confirmed the UK experienced its hottest summer since records began nearly 150 years ago.

Five heatwaves between May and August left the majority of the country in drought and have sparked wildfires and travel disruption.

The UK recorded a mean average temperature across June, July and August of 16.5C, beating the previous seasonal high of 16.1C set last year, the Met Office said.

The highest temperature recorded this summer was on 13 August at Kew Gardens, when the mercury hit 38.1C.

open image in gallery The capital will see temperatures of 23C on Saturday before it reaches 24C on Monday ( Met Office )

Changeable conditions with occasional rain or showers arriving from the North Atlantic, are set to be frequent in northern and western parts of the UK until the end of September, according to the Met Office.

But there will also be some dry and more settled periods in the south.

Towards the end of September high pressure may become more dominant bringing more settled conditions, with warmer daytime temperature and cooler nights.

Met Office five day forecast

Today:

Heavy rain slowly clearing the southeast in the morning. A brighter day for many and feeling fresh. Winds gradually easing in the north, with showers too.

Tonight:

Drier tonight with a few showers and plenty of clear spells. Lighter winds and feeling chilly, particularly in the countryside.

Wednesday:

Largely dry on Wednesday with plenty of sunny spells. Showers gradually easing along the east coast. Temperatures around or slightly below average for the time of year.

Outlook for Thursday to Saturday:

Drier and brighter on Wednesday with spells of sunshine. Another band of rain then moves in for Thursday, before drier and brighter weather returns on Friday. Temperatures likely around average.

News.title: The Chancellor’s speech, as it happened
News.content:
John Healey failed to rule out tax rises at next month’s Budget in his first major speech as Chancellor.

Mr Healey also sought to blame Liz Truss and her mini-Budget in 2022 for the high borrowing costs being paid by the Treasury.

During a speech in Coventry, the Chancellor said he would be “honest” about the need to control public spending during his time in Number 11.

He was speaking days after the cost of government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007.

It was also overshadowed by Jaguar Land Rover announcing plans to cut 4,000 jobs in the face of “intense competition and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty”.

Read our report on the Chancellor’s speech.

News.title: Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week
News.content:
At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

News.title: Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions
News.content:
This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

News.title: Antonelli walks on water while Hamilton rages from mountaintop
News.content:
The 20-year-old also benefited from a perfectly-timed (from his perspective at least) mid-race virtual safety car when Lance Stroll retired his Aston Martin, which allowed Antonelli a cheap stop to switch to fresh mediums while Russell stayed out on used hards. But at some point you just have to take your hat off to the youngster.

Antonelli was irresistible. He had already surged from 19th on the grid to 12th by the time the red flag came out at the end of lap 2. He was up to sixth a couple of laps after the race resumed. And by lap 18 of a 53-lap race, he had passed Russell for the lead for the first time. That is some going.

Having caught up to Russell, the two Mercedes drivers engaged in an entertaining battle for a few laps, the pair of them yo-yoing in and out of the lead before Russell got past Antonelli on lap 23 and managed to make it stick.

But the key moment of the race came on lap 27 when Stroll stopped at the first chicane and the VSC came out. For Antonelli, the decision to switch to fresh mediums was clear. He was going to struggle to make it to the end of the race. Far better to drop a few positions and fight back on fresh rubber.

For Russell, it was far trickier. He was in the lead of the race. He was on hard tyres which he knew could get to the end of the race. And he also had the problem of Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, who at the time he was struggling to shake off.

Mercedes chose to keep Russell out there. In hindsight, it may have been the wrong decision. Had he stopped at that point, he would at least have stayed ahead of Antonelli, and on the same tyres. By staying out, he kept the lead but found himself relentlessly hunted down by the Italian.

By lap 49, the Italian had caught up to him. Antonelli botched his first attempt at reclaiming the lead, going wide onto the gravel at the first chicane. But he made no mistake one lap later as Russell was once again left licking his wounds.

News.title: VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling
News.content:
“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

News.title: Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw
News.content:
A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

News.title: Relentless Springboks give All Blacks 15 minutes of hell to lead series
News.content:
There will be no repeat of the All Blacks historic Test series victory in South Africa 30 years ago, after the home side ruthlessly ensured they will lead 2-1 going into the concluding weekend.

And the manner in which the Springboks blew away their fierce rivals in the last 15 minutes made Rassie Eramus’s men overwhelming favourites to finish the job in America next Saturday.

However, there were passages of this brutal battle that suggested that Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry could still produce a finale worthy of the billing if New Zealand can learn the lessons from this brutal encounter at the FNB Stadium in Johannesburg.

There was a late Kiwi try to give the scoreboard a humdinger hue but Erasmus’s side were well deserving of their second victory in as many Saturdays over their fierce rivals, and credit to the South Africa coach for outwitting counterpart Dave Rennie without needing to change his starting XV just before the kick-off, like he did seven days before.

Amazing what one can do with a simple but chilling game plan. The old scoundrel knew that if he slowed it down and let his scrum walk round the All Blacks scrum that his backs would have the precious space.

Yet, however it might feel away from Springbok turf, New Zealand will still fancy their chances of levelling it, especially after matching their opponents’ haul of four tries. Their fly-half, Ruben Love, missed five simple-enough points and until that last quarter it was an even contest. Yet, as it tends to, South Africa’s physical intensity and their almighty scrum eventually prevailed.

News.title: Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

Sports.title: ‘He might be a centre-half’ – Souness bizarrely rips into Declan Rice and names 4 teams Arsenal star wouldn’t get into
Sports.content:
GRAEME SOUNESS has once again bizarrely laid into Declan Rice – who he reckons is playing out of his true position.

The Liverpool legend lambasted Rice after England‘s World Cup semi-final exit to Argentina, branding him a “limited” player.



And the Scot also claimed the Arsenal midfielder “WON’T GET ANY BETTER“.

Rice was, in the eyes of many, one of England’s best performers at the World Cup and played an integral role in Arsenal ending their 22-year-long wait to lift the Premier League trophy last season.



But Souness has doubled down on his stance on the midfielder, who he reckons is a de facto centre-back.

During an appearance on Piers Morgan‘s Football Uncensored show, he said: “How many times do you see him as the last man with the ball.



“In the build-up, he’s last man. He’s sitting between two centre-halves or between the centre-half and the full-back. He’s last man.

“A lot of the time, he doesn’t play in midfield. ‘In my second or third home game (of my career), I went into the back four like all midfield players do today. It’s old man’s football. It’s cheating.

” An old man’s way of playing midfield. You get the ball under no pressure and you play it out to the full-back.”

Souness added: “He plays too deep to affect the game. I don’t think he’s got enough football. Let me tell you what he can do.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“He’s the best defensive midfielder in the country right now, he smells danger. But then again, he’s back there all the time.

“He’s not a midfield player then is he? I think he may be a centre-half.

“The ball travels faster than you do. I see him run with the ball 30 yards and pass it square.

“He’s a lovely kicker of the ball and opens his body up well, there’s nothing to dislike about him. But modern players are a bit precious.



“Criticism doesn’t fall easily on these [players’] shoulders. He isn’t the complete midfield player.”

Gunners superfan Morgan leapt to Rice’s defence, insisting the former West Ham man is a world class midfielder.

Souness firmlu replied: “I’m not sure if he gets in Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, Man City.



“If you want the best in that position, City had two of them – Fernandinho and Rodri.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“They played in midfield. Next time, please watch him. He goes in and gets it cheap under no pressure, a 10-yard pass off Gabriel, and passes it sideways.”

Rice and his Arsenal team-mates will be back in action tomorrow night, travelling to Naples to take on Napoli in their Champions League opener.

Sports.title: Man Utd ‘swoop to sign wonderkid, 16, from hated rivals Liverpool’ days after transfer window slammed shut
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED have swooped to sign Isaac Konde from Liverpool, according to reports.

Transfers between the Red Devils and the Reds are rare.



But Old Trafford chiefs have moved to land 16-year-old Konde from their fierce rivals.

SunSport reported in July how Man Utd were moving to land a trio of youngsters, including Konde.



And the transfer has now been given the “here we go” treatment from Fabrizio Romano.

The transfer expert reports the formal steps for the move have been completed, opening the door for the deal to be sealed.

Konde is a highly regarded winger with electric pace and strong dribbling skills.

He starred for Liverpool’s Under-18s last season.

The Anfield wonderkid is most at home on the left wing, but is more than capable of operating off the right flank and as a centre-forward.

Ineos have put a lot of emphasis on trying to poach high-potential talent from youngsters.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

To that end Man Utd also moved to sign former Manchester City duo David Eze and Karim Cassim.

With Konde joining the pair, it is understood they will all link up with Darren Fletcher’s Under-18 squad.

So far they have played three games in the Under-18 Premier League, beating Everton and Middlesbrough but losing their opener to Man City.

Michael Carrick’s senior team hasn’t fared any better, losing their opener against Hull before beating Ipswich and suffering a gut-wrenching draw at Everton on Sunday.

Sports.title: Newcastle must keep SELLING despite bringing in £228m this summer – with Man Utd set to go back in for Lewis Hall
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE must keep selling to achieve their 2030 vision.

The Mags recouped around £228m by selling captain Bruno Guimaraes plus fellow stars Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali.



While the Brazilian skipper’s £75m exit was unplanned, the £60.6m sale of last season’s top scorer Gordon was critical to the club falling foul of financial regulations.

Tonali’s £92.5m switch to Tottenham helped fund a spending spree for new signings as the Mags forked out £266.6m to bring in eight new recruits, all aged 24 or younger, to transform the squad for new boss Matthias Jaissle.



New CEO David Hopkinson, who ambitiously declared Newcastle want to be “in the debate about being the top club in the world” by 2030, has already brought in additional cash through commercial deals.

Sporting director Ross Wilson says there is also “headroom” for new additions in January if needed, but admits the realities are that Newcastle will have to cash in during future windows too.

He said: “We built a squad for the season. That doesn’t mean we might not make further alterations to it in January.

“If you want to be a successful club in the Premier League you have to trade players and if you don’t the chances are you won’t be a successful club in the Premier League.

“Particularly where the revenues of this club are in a phase where David and his team are making those revenues really, really grow.

“But without that if you don’t trade players you are going to get stuck.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Newcastle tied down Harvey Barnes and homegrown prodigy Lewis Miley to new long-term deals over the summer.

Manchester United want star left-back Lewis Hall, 21.

Despite being issued with a firm hands-off warning this summer, they are still set to launch a move for him next year.

However, Wilson hopes the England international will instead be the next player he convinces to commit his future to the club.

With talks ongoing over a new deal for Hall, Wilson said: “We comment on things like that when they’re done.



“It’s unhelpful to comment otherwise. We confirmed Harvey and Lewis when they were done – that’s the best way for us to operate in this space. It’s not helpful to speculate on these things.

“We hope they’re [star players] with us on our journey to 2030.

“But we’ve got a player trading model as well. Who knows what 2030 looks like in terms of the squad?



“I’m sure there’ll be players in the 2030 squad that aren’t in the 2026/7 squad – I hope there are anyway.

“Of course we want to have players here who are on a journey with us.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“But equally if some of those player’s journeys go at rapid speed they might go somewhere else.

“But, of course, that’s normal, that’s part of football.”

Sports.title: Ex-Liverpool player turned manager offers lifeline to Jadon Sancho and Raheem Sterling
Sports.content:
Ex-Liverpool player turned manager offers lifeline to Jadon Sancho and Raheem Sterling

Raheem Sterling and Jadon Sancho are among two of the most high profile free agents out there and former Liverpool man Jonjo Shelvey has opened the door for a move to Dubai

View 2 Images Raheem Sterling endured an underwhelming stint at Feyenoord (Image: Getty)

Jonjo Shelvey has offered surprising lifelines to Raheem Sterling and Jadon Sancho in Dubai with the duo still without clubs.

‌



The ex-Liverpool and Newcastle midfielder is now in charge of the Arabian Falcons, who have only been in existence for three years. They play in the second tier of the UAE league, but the names involved at the club have given them a notable presence.

‌



Shelvey is supported by ex-Crystal Palace and Southampton star Jason Puncheon, who serves as director of football, and the club already boast former Premier League players Danny Simpson and Ravel Morrison.

‌



The Arabian Falcons are seeking to add more star names with talkSport claiming that Sancho and Sterling are on their shortlist, should they want to make the move over to the Gulf state.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Shelvey has revealed that several big name free agents have been in contact, especially now English clubs have all but concluded their recruitment. He told Hawksbee and Jacobs: "There are a couple that have got in touch.

‌



"I don't really deal with that side of it. I am trying to manage the team because I want to get promoted this year. But it is a fantastic opportunity for people if that is what they are looking for at this stage of their career, or if they are struggling to get a club.

"Once the UK window shuts, you are scrambling for clubs, so we put out a call to see if there was anyone who was interested. There are no strings attached to it. They can leave and go to bigger clubs whenever they are ready. But we can offer that Dubai lifestyle, and bigger names are coming out here."

View 2 Images Jadon Sancho is currently without a club (Image: 2026 James Gill - Danehouse)

‌



Sancho has found himself out in the cold, which represents a huge decline for a player who five years ago was costing Manchester United £72million. He had a host of Europe's top clubs eyeing him when he was impressing at Borussia Dortmund, but has never come close to replicating that form.

Successive loan spells away have failed to lead to an upturn in form and he now finds himself looking for a club. Sterling is another English talent who once thrived, but has endured a notable fall from grace.

Under Pep Guardiola at Manchester City, Sterling played the best football of his career but since moving to Chelsea in 2023 his career has continued to nosedive. His struggles continued in the Netherlands with Feyenoord, who chose not to retain him.

Sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold set for timely Liverpool reunion amid Real Madrid woes
Sports.content:
Trent Alexander-Arnold set for timely Liverpool reunion amid Real Madrid woes

Trent Alexander-Arnold is continuing to struggle out in Spain under Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid

View 2 Images The faltering defender will reunite with ex-Red Curtis Jones this week (Image: Darren Staples / AFP via Getty Images)

Trent Alexander-Arnold will reunite with fellow Liverpool academy graduate Curtis Jones in the Champions League on Tuesday, when Real Madrid host Inter Milan at the Santiago Bernabeu.

‌



Alexander-Arnold has started just one game for Real this season, assisting against Malaga in a 4-0 win. The defender has continued his struggle for consistent performances out in Spain after leaving Liverpool last year.

‌



Meanwhile, Jones has been enjoying life in Italy despite playing just 70 minutes so far. The midfielder came on in the second half against Napoli this weekend and, despite going 2-0 down, helped Inter deliver a comeback and win 3-2, maintaining the club's 100 per cent record this season.

‌



Discussing the victory, Jones said: "I'm absolutely over the moon. I am so happy to be part of a team and a club like this. It was obviously a hard game, but the lads stuck to the game plan. The fans were great throughout the whole match, and that is why we won."

Liverpool seal new signing days after window shut ahead of January arrival READ MORE :

Over in Spain, Alexander-Arnold came on for the last 30 minutes against Real Betis and watched Kylian Mbappe's penalty get saved as they fell to a 1-0 loss on the weekend. Both former Reds are off to different starts this season, but this reunion will likely come at the perfect time for the elder academy graduate.

Jose Mourinho has long-term plans for the defender, stating that he believes Alexander-Arnold is better suited to playing with new signing Yan Diomande. He told AS: "The team has always been good. I haven't seen the stats, but we created a lot. We missed three or four clear chances and their goalkeeper made three or four impressive saves.

‌



"I didn't make changes because I wasn't happy; they were to take off the players who had been booked. It's better to play with Trent and Yan Diomande than with Denzel Dumfries."

Sports.title: Dominik Szoboszlai sends Liverpool Premier League title warning with Steven Gerrard message
Sports.content:
Dominik Szoboszlai sends Liverpool Premier League title warning with Steven Gerrard message

Liverpool vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai has opened up to Steven Gerrard about the key change Liverpool must make under new head coach Andoni Iraola to mount a title challenge this season

View Image Dominik Szoboszlai has spoken at length to Steven Gerrard (Image: TNT Sports)

Dominik Szoboszlai says "no-one can stop" Liverpool if they raise their intensity this season under Andoni Iraola. The Reds' vice-captain admits it was sorely lacking during the failed defence of their Premier League crown last term, which ultimately cost Arne Slot his job.

‌



Liverpool finished 25 points behind champions Arsenal, who managed just one more point than the Reds did in their title-winning campaign. Szoboszlai, 25, was one of the few players to really impress at Anfield.

‌



Iraola has appointed the midfielder as one of his vice-captains as a result. He has now spoken to Steven Gerrard ahead of their first Champions League game of the season.

‌



Man Utd strike deal to land Liverpool wonderkid in major transfer coup READ MORE :

Steve McManaman explains Trent Alexander-Arnold issues as Jose Mourinho mulls over change READ MORE :

When quizzed about Iraola by Gerrard for TNT Sports, Szoboszlai said: "I like him [Iraola], I like him a lot. I know his playing style is really direct and intense, which I love, and I think that's the most important."

The former Reds skipper pressed further, asking whether intensity would be the key difference in his side's displays compared to last season. Szoboszlai replied: "I think it has to change."

"This is what we missed last season. If we can bring this intensity back, that we want it more than the others, we have the quality, and this, together, no one can stop us."

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

He also lifted the lid on what Iraola has already made clear about his role this season. Szoboszlai says: "I think he made it clear one time that I'm not going to play right-back.

"Which meant a lot to me (laughs). But if he needs me there, obviously, I'm gonna be available."

‌



Reflecting on the variety of roles he filled last season, the Hungary international said: "The only position I really didn't like was the 7." When quizzed about his preferred position on the pitch, Szoboszlai replied: "8 - like a box-to-box 8. Get the balls from the defender, give the long passes.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Concern over summer transfer already as two more exits confirmed
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Concern over summer transfer already as two more exits confirmed

Liverpool may have finally clicked on the pitch but there is currently much uncertainty off it

View 3 Images Richard Hughes has joined Al-Hilal (Image: Robin Jones/Getty Images)

The Andoni Iraola era at Liverpool finally kicked into gear over the weekend and he will now hope that form translates into the Champions League on Wednesday night. The Reds confidently disposed of Ipswich Town In Iraola's third game in charge, with Alexander Isak netting a brace, following two draws.

‌



The Basque manager will be taking on his very first game in Europe's premier competition as the mood around Anfield has been transformed thanks to the victory over the Tractor Boys. However, there are some causes for concern as the disruption off the field continues.

‌



Sporting director Richard Hughes has left the club for Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal and Liverpool have also sanctioned two more exits. Elsewhere, there may be growing concern over a player just a few games into the season. Mirror Football takes a closer look.

‌



Two more exits confirmed

While Al-Hilal have confirmed the appointment of Hughes, Mark Burchill and Craig McKee, who moved to Liverpool with Hughes in the summer of 2024, have also left for the Saudi-based side.

The duo had worked alongside chief scout Barry Hunter in the recruitment department, overseeing the club's transfer business during the 2025 and 2026 transfer windows.

Steve McManaman explains Trent Alexander-Arnold issues as Jose Mourinho mulls over change READ MORE :

Ex-Liverpool and Newcastle ace vindicated after wife refused to move for transfer READ MORE :

At Al-Hilal, Burchill will serve as director of recruitment, while McKee will serve as the club's director of scouting. Official confirmation of Hughes' move came a day after it was made public that he would be stepping down from his role at Anfield, after he joined from Bournemouth two seasons ago.

‌



View 3 Images Richard Hughes has left Liverpool (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Fenway Sports Group president Mike Gordon is overseeing the search for a new sporting director. In a statement on their official website on Sunday evening, Al-Hilal said: "The appointment of Hughes came as part of Al-Hilal's efforts to strengthen its football system and develop its sporting structure with specialised expertise.

"This will contribute to raising the quality of technical work, developing recruitment and scouting processes, and enhancing integration across all aspects related to the football sector."

‌

Liverpool may have some early concerns over Ifeanyi Ndukwe's loan spell at Levante, with the young defender yet to make an appearance. The 18-year-old made a switch to La Liga in the summer transfer window in an attempt to gain some experience, as well as the opportunity to become eligible for a work permit.

‌



The centre-back impressed during Liverpool's pre-season, starting every game. For all three matches of his loan so far, Ndukwe has remained on the bench, with Adrian Dela and Aissa Mandi preferred.

View 3 Images Ndukwe was signed from Austria Wien earlier this year (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Ndukwe's loan was essentially forced upon the Reds, as the club were unable to secure a work permit for the defender due to his lack of top-flight experience. Work permits are granted through a Governing Body Endorsement (GBE), which means the player must earn enough points to play in certain competitions.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford sent transfer message as Gary Neville highlights 'massive mistake'
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford sent transfer message as Gary Neville highlights 'massive mistake'

Manchester United were held to a 2-2 draw at Everton on Sunday afternoon but their Champions League opener is now on the horizon

View 3 Images Michael Carrick's Manchester United drew 2-2 with Everton in the Premier League (Image: Getty)

Manchester United were held to a 2-2 draw after conceding a last-minute equaliser against Everton. But Michael Carrick's side must quickly shift their attention to a Champions League tie with Sabah FK.

‌



Having been beaten by Hull City 2-0 to begin their Premier League season, United's fortunes were turned around with a 5-2 victory against Ipswich Town. Carrick's men then visited Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday, hopeful of getting a result. A sublime Bryan Mbeumo finish put them 1-0 up early in the second half.

‌



The Toffees hit back eight minutes from time through Tyrique George, though Benjamin Sesko thought he'd won United the game in the 87th minute. But in the sixth minute of added time, the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles on the edge of the United box and his long-range strike beat Senne Lammens.

‌



Gary Neville has singled out Patrick Dorgu for his role in the late equaliser. The Dane only entered the field of play in the 70th minute for Marcus Rashford, who has been sent a telling message regarding his loan spell at Barcelona. Mirror Football brings you the latest out of Old Trafford ahead of United's Thursday night European tie.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Marcus Rashford's Barcelona message

Rashford, who started his second consecutive league fixture on Sunday, took to Instagram after Everton held United with a statement to his 22.3 million followers.

‌



View 3 Images Rashford reacted to the game on his social media account (Image: Getty)

"So unlucky not to come away with all the points today! The results will come. Big week coming up starting with Thursday's game," he wrote.

And significantly, in the comments were two of his team-mates from his loan stint with Barcelona: Roony Bardghji and Fermin Lopez. Bardghji commented: "Man like Rashy" whilst Fermin simply posted a clapping hands and love-heart eyes emoji.

‌



The two evidently have not forgotten about the 28-year-old, who was linked with a permanent move back to the Camp Nou after his spell, and would likely have wanted him to return based on this affection. But the forward has ultimately stayed put to try and rebuild his United career under Carrick.

Dorgu, who replaced Rashford against Everton, has been criticised by ex-United defender Neville, who believes his errant pressing was a primary reason for the late goal being conceded.

‌



View 3 Images Neville singled out Dorgu as well as Santos and Leny Yoro (Image: Getty)

On his The Gary Neville Podcast, the Sky Sports pundit broke down the final stages of the game that led to Maitland-Niles scoring the equaliser. He said: "That last goal is a really bad one. Dorgu, for some reason, chases out and presses – isolated press. Andrey Santos then doesn't go cover behind him and stays back.

"It just gets played past Dorgu. It's a massive mistake that. It's a massive mistake from Dorgu but he might have been told to go press by Santos. But it just strikes me as a lack of communication."

Sports.content:
Man Utd strike deal to land Liverpool wonderkid in major transfer coup

Manchester United have struck an agreement with Liverpool to sign teenage star Isaac Konde as the 16-year-old prepares to move from Anfield to Old Trafford

View 2 Images Isaac Konde is set to swap Liverpool for Man Utd

Manchester United are said to have secured a deal to sign Liverpool's teenager Isaac Konde. The 16-year-old has completed the formal steps ahead of his move to Old Trafford, according to reports.

‌



Landing young talent from one of your rivals has become an increasingly common thing in recent years and the Red Devils have secured a deal to sign Konde, who has made six appearances for Liverpool so far this season in the Under-18s Premier League, coming up with one assist.

‌



Konde primarily operates off the left flank in the final third, but is equally effective on the opposite wing. He is a product of Liverpool's academy, but will now head to their rivals in the north west.

‌



Liverpool's biggest academy success of the last decade has been Trent Alexander-Arnold, but he left last summer for Real Madrid. Now they have the likes of Rio Ngumoha and Conor Bradley in their ranks.

United have a long history of giving youth a chance, but equally as they look to become a force once more huge sums have been spent on adding ready made first-team quality. Kobbie Mainoo has become a mainstay, but even he is having to fight to secure regular minutes.

‌



In pre-season Michael Carrick handed minutes to a host of the club's teenage stars, many of whom will hope to push on this season. Shea Lacey and Jack Fletcher both got run outs and were used last term.

They also landed Chido Obi, then 16, after he turned down the offer of an Arsenal extension to move to Manchester. His progress has since stalled and he headed out on loan late in the summer transfer window.

Sports.title: VAR row takes fresh twist as new image of Nottingham Forest disallowed goal released
Sports.content:
VAR row takes fresh twist as new image of Nottingham Forest disallowed goal released

Nottingham Forest's disallowed goal on Saturday has caused plenty of debate after Neco Williams was pinned for handball - but a new image has shed light on the saga

View 2 Images Nottingham Forest were left fuming after VAR ruled out their goal against Tottenham

A new picture shows the ball DID hit Neco Williams’ arm - but might not end the VAR row over Nottingham Forest ’s disallowed goal.

‌



Williams bundled the ball over the line but video assistant referee Peter Bankes disallowed the goal even though Forest boss Oliver Glasner insisted there was no proof.

‌



But a still picture does show the ball hitting Forest defender Williams’ arm which is why it was disallowed in Saturday’s goalless draw with Tottenham, denying the home side a precious win.

‌



However, the picture was not available to Bankes when he made his decision to intervene which then saw referee Craig Pawson disallow the goal.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Referees' body, Pro Ref, are comfortable that the correct decision was made and that Bankes is an experienced VAR who also knows tell-tale signs like a ripple of the shirt.

‌



Refs boss Howard Webb has overseen a “lighter touch” this season from VAR which should result in less interventions with the strict instructions that officials should not get involved unless they are sure. Pro Ref are backing the officials over this decision which has caused a backlash from Forest who have history on ref rows.

This time, Glasner said: “I think the VAR can't intervene when he is guessing. It was not clear and obvious. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high, which is why this is a wrong intervention.”

View 2 Images A new angle has shown that the ball did strike Neco Williams' arm

‌



The Forest boss also claimed: "I think it was a clear penalty when Neco Williams was fouled by Mo Kudus. We didn't feel that some decisions were in our favor today. If it's not 100% clear, stick to the on-field decisions. This is the inconsistency today. I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood."

The stats show that there have been just two subjective interventions this season which is a ratio of 0.06 after 30 games compared to 0.15 last season.

Arsenal had a goal ruled out by VAR in their win over Chelsea on Sunday. It came when they were trailing 1-0 but replays showed the officials were again right to step in.

Sports.title: Harry Kane tipped to join 'exclusive little club' and end 25-year wait with Ballon d'Or win
Sports.content:
Harry Kane tipped to join 'exclusive little club' and end 25-year wait with Ballon d'Or win

Harry Kane is set to be bang in contention for the Ballon d'Or, with Michael Owen already tipping him to win the award ahead of the likes of Kylian Mbappe

View 2 Images Harry Kane smiles as he warms up ahead of the 2026 World Cup football tournament third-place match between France and England at the Miami Stadium in Miami on July 18, 2026. (Photo by ROBERTO SCHMIDT / AFP via Getty Images) (Image: Getty)

Harry Kane has been told he deserves to join an “exclusive little club” - and be crowned winner of the Ballon D’Or.

‌



England captain Kane, 33, will discover his rivals for the prestigious crown on Tuesday when the 30 name shortlist is unveiled for one of the biggest honours in football.

‌



Kane is the red-hot bookies’ favourite after his record-breaking season when he scored 73 goals for club and would be England’s first winner in a quarter of a century.

‌



Michael Owen was the last winner in 2001 and believes Kane - who will be up against the likes of Rodri, Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi - deserves to win the award which will be handed out in London on October 26.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The Former Liverpool striker insists that Kane has had a “phenomenal season” and is the “best finisher on the planet. Owen said: “Let's hope that all that means that you're going to get a huge shout of winning the Ballon D’Or. I would welcome you with open arms to join our exclusive little club.”

‌



The Ballon D’Or often goes to a player from the winning nation in World Cup year but there is not an outstanding candidate and there is a strong feeling it could - and should - be Kane’s year, especially after a hugely successful season with Bayern Munich.

Kane, in an interview with TNT Sports, said: “I'm here now, and I'm winning awards like the Golden Shoe. And the Ballon d’Or is the same. Of course, now it's out of my hands in terms of it's down to the voters and the people who decide it.

View 2 Images Kylian Mbappe also has his sights set on the prestigious award (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



“The season I had was my best season by far, and we have to wait and see this. It's a weird one because I'm already focussed on this season now and the next season and thinking how can I be better, how can I improve. But also I want to appreciate what I did. Time will tell.”

Real Madrid star Mbappe is also banging the drum for his own cause as he is dreaming of winning it for the first time even though he did not win any trophies.

Mbappe said: “I think when you play for Real Madrid, the best club in the world, people associate you with this award. There are many people that speak about me and the Ballon d'Or. Of course I've made history in the most important competition. Maybe it's a good year for this but people can vote according to what they think.”

Sports.title: Newcastle chief: Summer was 'not chaotic' with Howe exit prepared for
Sports.content:
Newcastle sporting director Ross Wilson says they were "prepared for a number of months" for Eddie Howe's exit in a summer that "never felt chaotic".

Howe's shock resignation in July led to the swift appointment of Matthias Jaissle, who has enjoyed an unbeaten start to his reign.

Howe's exit was part of a turbulent summer for the Magpies which also included the departures of key players Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon.



Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Keith Downie explains the three things we learned from Newcastle's 2-2 draw against Bournemouth

Toon chief Wilson revealed Howe's resignation was not "painful" because of their Jaissle contingency, but Guimaraes' £75m move to Arsenal was not "part of the plan".

Wilson said: "Eddie is an exceptionally talented coach and at some point that meant he was probably going to do something else and we had to be prepared for that.

"It didn't feel painful. Clearly the timing was not one we had planned for. But we had a plan in place which is why we executed it as quickly as we did.

"It might have caught some people off guard, but the reason we could move so quickly on it was because we had prepared for a number of months."

Leeds United

Newcastle United Monday 14th September 6:30pm Kick off 8:00pm

Wilson added: "I think we want Newcastle United to be a club with anticipation and excitement. If we're not it probably means we're doing it wrong.

"[This summer] never felt chaotic inside. There is no point us pretending otherwise - we did not want to lose Bruno Guimaraes. That was really disappointing that we got to that place in the end.

"We were happy where we got to in terms of numbers but that was not part of our plan. But everything else that happened during the window was part of the plan."

'Trading an important part of Newcastle plan'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jaissle gives his thoughts on new midfielder Nico Gonzalez

Wilson believes success for Newcastle rests on them being a trading club going forwards after a summer of fluctuating fortunes in the transfer window.

Newcastle raised nearly £250m in player sales but signed eight players aged 24 or under, with much enthusiasm over the big-money arrivals of Nico Gonzalez and Matias Fernandez-Pardo.

"If you want to be a successful club in the Premier League, you have to trade players and if you don't the chances are you won't be a successful club in the Premier League," said Wilson.

"This is what we've got to do. And if you don't do it, then just keep the squad you've got and forevermore they'll grow old, achieve less and leave for nothing."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player European football expert Julien Laurens explains why Mathias Fernandez-Pardo's arrival made sense for Newcastle

The outlook is shaped by Newcastle being fined £5.2m for breaching UEFA's financial sustainability regulations, with £6m suspended pending future compliance.

They have not qualified for Europe this season, and chief financial officer Simon Capper has forecast the club will be "compliant" with the more relaxed Premier League financial rules.

Woltemade exit allowed Fernandez-Pardo signing

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jaissle revealed new signing Fernandez-Pardo had settled in quickly

Wilson and Capper also revealed that club-record signing Nick Woltemade had to leave on loan to allow the arrival of Fernandez-Pardo.

On Deadline Day, Woltemade, who joined last summer in a £69m deal, moved to Juventus on loan, with Newcastle confirming the £51m signing of Fernandez-Pardo from Lille.

Wilson said: "Because we try to link things together, the ultimate deal for Fernandez-Pardo was only possible because we did the Woltemade deal. The ultimate [Fernandez-Pardo] deal.

"If we didn't do the Woltemade deal, we might have done another deal, but that's what we mean by linking things together."

Capper added: "So the conversation we were having internally was, 'If you want to do that [sign Fernandez-Pardo] you're going to have to give me something back…otherwise we'll be in a position we're not comfortable with'.

"We managed to get that. That's how we work together as a group, as a senior management team, to deliver the best result we can out of a transfer window."

Sports.title: Should England rotate bowlers or be ruthless in final Pakistan Test?
Sports.content:
As a Test summer during which English cricket appeared to be in crisis nears its end, Joe Root's side go into their final fixture against Pakistan with the only major talking point being whether the bowling attack will be rotated.

Barring the discovery of any more England off-field issues before the start of the third Test at Edgbaston on Wednesday, it's Pakistan making all the noise after sacking their head coach and replacing seven members of their touring squad following defeats at Headingley and Lord's.

Brydon Carse remains absent from England's 15-player group at Edgbaston after the fast bowler was briefly arrested following an incident outside a Derby nightclub in August. Fellow quick Matthew Fisher has been dropped, but the rest of the group were all part of the squad at Lord's last time out.

With a series victory sealed, England could choose to give some of their cross-format players a rest ahead of upcoming white-ball contests with Sri Lanka.

If the third Test were to go all five days, the first of three T20 internationals would start just two days later, before three 50-over matches follow later in September.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook caught Mohammad Ali off the bowling of Josh Tongue to complete England's 194-run victory over Pakistan at Lord's and seal a series win with a game to spare

Perhaps the biggest positive to come out of the series so far has been the performance of England's new-look pace attack, made up of Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson, Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue.

Three of the four are also part of both England's T20 and ODI squads to face Sri Lanka, with only Robinson not currently part of the white-ball setup.

Ahead of England revealing their final Test XI of the summer, Sky Sports assess whether the incumbents should be rested, and the merits of those who could replace them.

The incumbents

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jofra Archer dismissed Babar Azam for six with a vicious rising delivery as Pakistan slipped to 14-3 in their chase of 389 at Lord's

Jofra Archer - England's star bowler has had a very encouraging summer fitness wise, performing at a consistently high level in the four out of five Tests he's played in.

Given Archer only returned to Test cricket last summer after more than four years out of the longest form of the game, England would be wise to take every opportunity to maintain the 31-year-old's freshness.

Speaking to the media on Monday, Archer said: "My body is in a good place, the team is in a good place, and everyone is in a good place. I just want to play cricket."

While it's good to hear him say such things, there is no doubt that a fit Archer walks straight into any England XI, so the focus should be on ensuring that's the condition he remains in ahead of next summer's home Ashes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gus Atkinson took the final wicket when England defeated New Zealand in the first Test at Lords

Gus Atkinson - The Surrey quick has also played four out of five Tests so far this summer, with his only absence coming when he was made unavailable for selection for the second Test against New Zealand after being involved in an incident at a nightclub, alongside former skipper Ben Stokes.

Atkinson hasn't bowled badly by any means against Pakistan, but has had little reward, claiming just one of the 38 Pakistan wickets that have fallen across the two games.

With that in mind, there is a strong argument that of the three quicks also playing white-ball cricket, Atkinson should be given another opportunity to fill his boots against a fragile Pakistan batting line-up before returning to Test action against South Africa in December.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Josh Tongue dismissed Abdullah Shafique and Babar Azam on day two of England's second Test against Pakistan

Josh Tongue - The Nottinghamshire quick is the only member of England's bowling attack to have played all five Tests this summer.

Those performances, along with strong showings before that against Australia and India have made him undroppable for incoming head coach Stephen Fleming.

Bowling consistently up and around 90 miles per hour is not easy, and as with Archer, England would be wise to take the opportunity to rest this athlete before he is called upon with the white ball.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Robinson trapped Azan Awais lbw for six before bowling Abdullah Shafique for a duck three balls later as Pakistan slipped to 7-2 in their chase of 389 at Lord's

Ollie Robinson - The star of the series, Robinson has taken 16 Pakistan wickets at a remarkable average of just 7.18 and an economy of 2.05.

The same old injury issues appeared to have halted the momentum he built with a fine first Test performance against New Zealand in June, with knee soreness ruling him out of the next game before he was overlooked for the series finale.

Given the 32-year-old won't be playing white-ball cricket, he should embrace the opportunity to lead England's attack at Edgbaston and prove he's got the durability to complete a series, albeit one where the bowling attack have had things all their own way.

The contenders

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A delighted Sonny Baker took his first Test wicket against New Zealand during Day One of the Second Test at The Oval

Sonny Baker - Perhaps the most exciting member of England's fast bowling ranks at the age of just 23, Baker only got called up to the squad for the second Test at Lord's because of Carse's off-field antics. The fact he's been retained over Fisher suggests he at least impressed in the nets at Lord's, and stand-in coach Marcus Trescothick could now reward him.

Baker had a challenging debut when England were in crisis for the second Test against New Zealand, managing match figures of just 3-161 in the defeat at The Oval.

Given the selectors can never be sure when injuries might hit and Baker could be needed, allowing him the opportunity to get more Test experience and build his confident in this fixture could be a smart move.

However, the fact he is also in England's white-ball squads to face Sri Lanka means opportunities can also be given to him in those formats.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A delighted Sam Cook took his first-ever Test wicket against Zimbabwe during day two of their one-off test against England

Sam Cook - Similarly to Baker, Cook has just one Test appearance to his name - that didn't go very well.

The Essex quick struggled to make an impact as he took just one wicket during England's victory over Zimbabwe at Trent Bridge in May 2025.

However, he's put together another impressive County Championship campaign, taking 39 wickets in nine matches at an average of just over 19.

At the age of 29, he possesses less room for development than Baker, and would appear to be an option for sooner rather than later. For that reason, it could be argued it makes sense to give him another opportunity to prove himself this week.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Shoaib Bashir takes the wicket of Rachin Ravindra on day four of the third Test between England and New Zealand

Shoaib Bashir - England's lead spinner doesn't turn 23 until October, but has already been through quite a bit during his international career.

Fast-tracked into the side by Ben Stokes and Brendon McCullum in 2024, Bashir was being prepared for England's trip to Australia last winter, but then surprisingly didn't feature in any of the five Tests.

That saga looked as though it may put his Test career on hold, but Bashir was selected again this summer and played in two Tests against New Zealand. He wasn't needed at Lord's, but then struggled at Trent Bridge as he returned match figures of 3-147.

A spinner is often deemed necessary at Edgbaston, but with spin not necessarily a key factor for England's big upcoming Test series in South Africa this winter and at home to Australia next summer, assessing the pace options may be seen as a priority.

Sports.title: How Calafiori has become 'the best left-back in the league by far'
Sports.content:
Riccardo Calafiori returns to Italy with Arsenal this week - and he's a very different player compared to the one who departed for England two years ago.

When Arsenal came in for Calafiori, he was regularly playing at centre-back at Bologna. Those who guided his career had doubts about whether he could reach the highest level as a left-back.

But now, Calafiori is not just thriving as a left-back for the Premier League champions. "He's the best left-back in the league by far," says Jamie Carragher.

As well as being part of an imperious Arsenal defence, the Italian has started this season on fire in front of goal, scoring in the Community Shield win over Manchester City and getting assists in the league victories over Coventry and Aston Villa.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Arsenal and Chelsea.

VAR spotting an offside Ezri Konsa denied Calafiori getting on the scoresheet against Chelsea, but the Italian did have a crucial role in Arsenal's winning goal, scored by Martin Odegaard.

In the build-up, Calafiori's run inside of Christos Tzolis helped drag Pedro Neto into a back five - putting more Chelsea players behind the ball and rubberstamping Arsenal's dominance on the game.

Image: Calafiori (circled) helped push Chelsea's Pedro Neto (also circled in blue) into the back five

"He dictated the formation of Chelsea," said Carragher, analysing the goal on Sky Sports. "Wherever Calafiori was, Neto was. When Calafiori drops forward, Neto drops into make a back five.

"Chelsea were flittering between a back four in the main and a back five. It's all about the positioning of Calafiori."

But that was not all. Calafiori kept going.

His run into the penalty area then dragged centre-back Maxence Lacroix with him and created a 14.4-yard gap between the Chelsea defender and his partner Wesley Fofana.

Image: Calafiori created a 14.4 yard gap between Chelsea's centre-backs, allowing Odegaard to score

That was all the space Arsenal needed for Kai Havertz to dummy the ball to Odegaard, who finished with ease.

But again, that's not all. Because we've seen that exact same move from Arsenal before.

Arsenal's third goal in the Community Shield win over City had the same characteristics. A run and ball in from Tzolis, a dummy from Havertz - and Odegaard comfortably scoring.

But crucially, it had the same underlapping run made by Calafiori - which created the same large centre-back gap between Ruben Dias and Josko Gvardiol.

"You see the space between the centre-backs, that comes from Calafiori," added Carragher. "This is the impact he's having on games at left-back."

Image: Odegaard exploited a similar gap in the Man City defence to score vs Chelsea

But can his position really be described as 'left-back', given Calafiori is effectively operating as an extra attacker for this Arsenal team? The Italian has a habit of popping up everywhere, from centre forward to right wing.

It was seen in the first half against Chelsea, when Calafiori ventured from the left to the right flank in the same attacking move - taking just eight seconds to pop up in a completely different role.

Image: Calafiori starts a move in a more traditional left-back position

Image: Eight seconds later, Calafiori had ventured over to the right wing to collect a pass from Kai Havertz

"That's Ricci though!" said former Arsenal winger Leandro Trossard in November when asked by Sky Sports about Calafiori's wild positioning.

"He pops up everywhere - in the pockets, as a striker - that unpredictability can hurt teams.

"I know what he can do and where he can pop up in what position. Sometimes I can play a ball blind to him and I know he will be there."

Image: Calafiori was seen in the No 10 position in between Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz against Chelsea

It seems, on the basis of the goals Odegaard scored against Man City and Chelsea, that Calafiori has a similar understanding building with new winger Tzolis.

It is not just Calafiori who does this, as Ben White is also tasked with taking rogue positions in the Arsenal attack. He was also seen in a hybrid centre-forward role during the Chelsea game at times.

Image: Ben White was also seen in the centre forward role against Chelsea

While White tends to take the role of a more traditional full-back compared to Calafiori's maverick positioning, his tactical flexibility is summed up by the fact that he ranks top of overlapping runs in the Premier League this season, and fourth for underlapping runs.

"Playing full-back the way he [Mikel Arteta] wants is, I think, completely different to any other manager," White told Sky Sports in the 2023-24 season.

"To play full-back for him, you've got to be a centre mid, a centre-back, a winger and a No 10."

When fully fit, Arsenal are a well-oiled machine that are a nightmare to prepare for tactically. "They push you to the limits," said Xabi Alonso after his Chelsea team came away from the Emirates with a 2-1 defeat.

Every player has to be accounted for in defending. No player can be left unmarked or unwatched for long. Calafiori is the epitome of why Arsenal are so difficult to play against.

It shows why so many teams revert to a low block against Arsenal. There are so many attackers to play against. And if you try to take Arsenal on - thereby opening yourselves up in defence - you get what Chelsea got.

Sports.title: Why the F1 title race is not over yet...
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli's stunning Italian Grand Prix victory felt like a key moment in this year's championship as he landed a psychological blow on his title rivals by winning from 19th.

Antonelli now leads George Russell by 66 points, Lewis Hamilton by 76 points and Lando Norris by 96 points with 10 scheduled rounds remaining.

Without doubt, the Italian is favourite for the championship - and would be the youngest driver ever to become world champion should he do it - but the season is far from over yet...

Monza was a one-off track

The long straights at Monza put high emphasis on a strong power unit and Mercedes have been the benchmark in this department, even though the FIA ruled earlier this year that Red Bull have the best engine.

It is the deployment of the Mercedes though - which was not measured by the FIA - which stands out and they were effectively able to get more out of the electrical side of their power unit to excel on the straights.

There are no further tracks that will be reliant on the power unit to the extremity of Monza, although Baku later this month and Las Vegas in November feature long full throttle sections. However, both circuits have more corners than Monza.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Italian Grand Prix

"I'm quite happy, first of all, that we were able to perform in Monza like we did, because we weren't sure. Ferrari brought an engine upgrade and others on the chassis side, and this is a development race," said Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff.

"But we have to consider the fact that Monza is an outlier on the track. It's on one end, and then there is Monaco on the other."

This weekend's new race in Madrid is a complete unknown but the track layout looks very twisty and cars that are strong in the corners - which should suit McLaren and Ferrari - will be fast.

Azerbaijan follows, which can be a chaotic race, then the more traditional tracks of Sepang in Malaysia, Austin in the USA and the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in Mexico should see the field be much closer - depending on upgrades...

Formula 1 2026 remaining races Madrid September 11-13 Brazil November 6-8 Azerbaijan September 24-26 Las Vegas November 20-22 Malaysia October 2-4 Qatar November 27-29 Singapore* October 9-11 Abu Dhabi December 4-6 USA October 23-25 *denotes Sprint weekend Mexico Oct 30-Nov 1

Lots to play out in development race

The two races prior to Monza saw McLaren with a car that was capable of winning as Norris drove superbly to victory in Hungary and the Netherlands.

Most teams have gained big chunks of performance when fitting new parts to the car and Mercedes are not bringing any upgrades until Malaysia at the start of next month.

"We must not get ahead of ourselves now, thinking, 'well, we can wait for the upgrade until Malaysia'. We know that it's going to be a big fight in Madrid. Our car hasn't got the performance levels that it has in Monza for the next race in Madrid," said Wolff.

"We know that our upgrades would help a lot in Madrid but we haven't got them. So we just need to do our best and that could mean that some of the race weekends, not winning, but just scoring points."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli wins the Italian Grand Prix from 19th on the grid

McLaren boss Andrea Stella says the team's realistic target is to "consistently" be in the fight for wins until the end of the season.

"I think our tracks will be more the likes of Malaysia, Austin, Brazil. I think where we have some long corners, the car seems to express its potential well," said Stella.

"We have some new upgrades that we will take to Baku, but we still think that tracks like Baku and Madrid where you have to be very precise with the trajectory, short corners, maybe they don't play to the best of our car. Yet we have to say that in Zandvoort and Hungary we were in a position to win races and in Monza while we were not, we know that it's a special race.

"The drag will be less important in Madrid, there's a much higher density of corners, so we will definitely give it a go, but from a championship point of view I think we have to remain very realistic, don't get conditioned by looking at the classification, just focus on one race at a time."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player First look at F1's newest circuit - the 'Madring'

Will Antonelli crack under increasing pressure?

Right now the answer is a firm no. Antonelli is a generational talent with bundles of speed and it's his sheer pace which has made the difference this year.

He's only 20 years old though and in his second season, so most drivers would still be making costly mistakes at this stage of their career.

There has been no sign of that from Antonelli though but you would expect that he will be tested several times in the remaining races - whether that's due to the closeness of the field and being on the right side of the stopwatch, or a rainy Sunday where a small error can suddenly fire you into the barriers.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli reflects on his sensational 19th to first Monza victory, catching teammate George Russell to claim a landmark home win and strengthen his championship lead

"Definitely it's been a very strong year so far, but still many races left and so, still anything can happen," said Antonelli.

"And we've seen how things can swing very quickly. So, on my side, as I said many times, just take it race by race, focus on things that I can control and just maximise every opportunity I get.

"In Monza we were fastest, but we never know. We might go to another track and all of a sudden, McLaren is the fastest, or Ferrari is up there, or even Red Bull, with Max."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Italy's commentary when Kimi Antonelli won at Monza

Indeed, should McLaren or Ferrari suddenly have the fastest car for consecutive races, and Antonelli is not on the podium - Hamilton or Norris could gain double figures in points from one Grand Prix, then the pressure will inevitably ramp up too on Antonelli.

The outlook is actually bleaker for Russell as he has the same equipment as Antonelli but does not have the pace to match his team-mate.

It is harder to see how that changes, whereas - as Antonelli points out - McLaren or Ferrari may have the best car over the final 10 rounds.

Perhaps Wolff sums up best how the F1 title race stands when he stated: "It's motor racing. It's a technical sport. Things can break, accidents can happen and that's why we have to do our best job for both drivers. Continue to bring our best game."

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Roadlesstravelled makes chase debut at Bangor
Sports.content:
Jumps action from Bangor-on-Dee features live on Sky Sports Racing on Tuesday.

5.12 Bangor-on-Dee - Roadlesstravelled makes chase debut

Grade Two winner Roadlesstravelled makes his chase debut in the John Hewitt Memorial Novices' Limited Handicap Chase.

The seven-year-old began his career impeccably, winning three from three over hurdles, including a Grade Two novice hurdle. He has regressed markedly since, pulling up in the Formby Novices' Hurdle in December 2024, and has spent some time on the Flat since.

He ran too keen on his last Flat start and returns to obstacles to make his chase debut off nearly a four-month break. He won an Irish point-to-point quite takingly back in May 2023, so if Jonjo and AJ O'Neill have got him back in decent shape, he could run a solid race.

Captain Cool by far holds the most experience over fences and sets a solid standard with a BHA rating of 131. He can put that experience to good use and serve it up to the rest.

Krak seems on a handy mark if putting it altogether. He was beaten by 10 lengths last time out but did not seem to stay that day and could get back on track down in trip.

Ice In The Veins was beaten by 25 lengths to Captain Cool in June, and although it will be a tough task again, being better off at the weights and racing more economically will certainly bring them closer together.

11.55 Lyon-Parilly - San Giorgio and Master Man clash

San Giorgio and Master Man clash in the Listed Criterium de Lyon.

The Francis-Henri Graffard-trained San Giorgio is improving by the run, getting off the mark when battling well last time in a fair novice.

He holds strong form lines, finishing behind the current top French two-year-old Avec Toi, and perhaps showed most promise on his second start when running on behind a nice two-year-old in Ciceron.

Be My Friend was one place behind San Giorgio that day when making his debut. He seemed to come on for that run when winning in taking fashion next time out at Vichy, and he can prove a huge threat with more experience under his belt.

Master Man has held a consistently solid level of form, winning two of his three starts and perhaps sets the standard on what he has achieved thus far.

Skyridge narrowly beat Palais Byzantin in July and they should both be competitive, although lack the scope for improvement that the former three do.

5.42 Bangor-on-Dee - Hidden Fortune headlines

The promising Hidden Fortune headlines in the Paul Ferguson's Jumper To Follow Novices' Hurdle.

The Dan Skelton-trained five-year-old got off to a winning start over hurdles following two promising bumper seconds. She won impressively at the first attempt and contains a lot of scope for improvement, shaping last time as if longer trips and softer ground may see her to best effect, and she should prove tough to beat.

Perhaps the main threat comes in the form of Provision who broke his maiden last time out with a 10-length win. He is more exposed than Hidden Fortune but contains the experience needed to serve it up to the mare.

Ride Like A Girl has a similar profile to Provision and could bounce back to form, having disappointed on her last start.

Secret Beach makes his hurdle debut with a very fair level of form on the Flat, being rated 78. He might need the experience but may go well if taking to the obstacles for the first time.

Best of the rest

Lyon-Parilly - Informative maidens on the card.
