Then there’s the South African Institute for Entrepreneurship (SAIE). In their manifesto they say they’re not about handouts. Their goal is to shift people from the passivity of grants towards actively seeking out opportunities. One such example of their success is the City of Cape Town Urban Backyard Garden Project. This is the programme that trained Nicky Jafta, the Kraaifontein pensioner who now runs a thriving micro-farm.



TAFTA CEO Femada Shamam frames it as more than an income play on SASSA. “Learning business skills in the elder generation is a proactive approach to meeting their financial needs. It’s also helps ease loneliness and exclusion, with the added bonus of potential job creation in the surrounding community,” said Shamam. In time, the plan is to roll out sponsored startup funding for very promising ideas.

2026 SASSA MEANS AND ASSET TESTS

Both organisations realise it’s as much about belonging as it is earning extra money on the side. Image: File

Critical to earn money without losing your SASSA grant is sticking within the agency’s means and asset test. In 2026, a single applicant can earn up R112 200 a year, or R9 350 a month, without the agency raising a red flag. Likewise, your total assets must stay below R1 584 000. With the right training and opportunity, that’s real room for side income before SASSA looks twice.

Neither organisation is promising a get-rich-quick scheme. TAFTA offers structured mentorship. And SAIE is selling a mindset shift backed by hands-on, practical skills training. Both are aimed at the same quiet fear most elderly pensioners carry with them. Trying to earn a little more without losing what they already have. While still remaining relevant and connected within their community.

Click here to find out more about TAFTA and you can navigate to the SAIE’s Facebook page by clicking the link.

But what do you think? Do you earn money without losing your SASSA grant? Do you have any tips/contacts to share with our audience? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: Anak Krakatau erupts: What it means for SA travellers
World.content:
If Bali, Lombok or Jakarta feature anywhere on your travel calendar this month, you need to know: Indonesia’s most notorious volcano is having a moment, and it’s throwing regional air travel into chaos.

WHAT’S HAPPENING?

Anak Krakatau, meaning “child of Krakatau,” born from the crater of the volcano that reshaped world history in 1883 — kicked off a major eruptive phase late on 4 September. Since then it’s been putting on a genuinely alarming show: lava fountains, booming rumbles heard for kilometres, and ash plumes rocketing up to 50,000 feet into the sky above the Sunda Strait, the narrow channel between Java and Sumatra.

The volcano remains at Alert Level III — the second-highest rung on Indonesia’s four-level warning scale — with a 3km exclusion zone in force around the crater. The good news, if you can call it that: authorities say there’s no tsunami threat, and the nearest settlement sits more than 16km away.



WHY THIS MATTERS

Ash and jet engines do not mix, and Indonesia’s aviation network has taken a serious hit. Eight airports — including Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta, the region’s second-busiest — shut down over the weekend as ash drifted across western Indonesia. By Monday, the transport ministry was reporting more than 1,500 flights cancelled, delayed or diverted, and upward of 270 000 passengers stranded.

Bali’s Ngurah Rai airport has so far avoided a full closure, but it hasn’t escaped unscathed — flights in from Jakarta have been cancelled and schedules shuffled as airlines reroute aircraft around the ash clouds. Medan has also felt the knock-on effects.

The volcano is still active and unpredictable, so more disruption down the line isn’t off the table. Indonesian officials have even floated cloud-seeding to try to rain the ash out of the sky faster.

WHAT THIS MEANS IF YOU’RE PLANNING TO TRAVEL

Flying via Jakarta to connect onward? Build in buffer time, or brace for it. Most South Africans heading to Bali route through Perth, Singapore, or occasionally Jakarta — check which leg of your itinerary passes through affected airspace and confirm directly with your airline rather than assuming your flight is unaffected.

Already booked a Bali or Lombok trip? Nothing suggests you should cancel outright — Bali itself is operating, and there’s no threat to the island. But do keep a close eye on your airline’s app and the airport’s own channels in the days before you fly, since schedules are shifting fast.

Wondering about travel insurance? Cover for weather and natural-disaster disruption typically depends on when you bought the policy relative to the eruption becoming public knowledge — buy it now expecting the volcano to bail you out, and most insurers will treat it as a “known event” excluded from cover. If you already had a policy in place before 4 September, you’re in a stronger position. Either way, keep every receipt for rebooking, meals or accommodation you’re forced to pay for.



Thinking of visiting the volcano itself? Don’t. The exclusion zone is there for a reason, and Anak Krakatau has a well-earned reputation — its 2018 eruption triggered an underwater landslide and a tsunami that killed over 400 people. This isn’t the moment for volcano tourism.

You will not need to entirely scrap your Indonesia plans over this, but flexibility is crucial. Check your specific route, monitor your airline directly rather than relying on general news, and don’t book anything non-refundable until the ash settles — literally.

World.title: PSL transfer window: Biggest winners and losers so far
World.content:
Only a few weeks remain in the Premier Soccer League transfer window.

So far in the 2026/27 season, we have already seen twists, turns, and headline moves.

This week, Golden Arrows beat Kaizer Chiefs to the signature of Zimbabwean international Jonah Fabisch.



Which teams have gained or lost the most in the PSL transfer window?

Winner: Kaizer Chiefs

Under head coach Fernando da Cruz, the Naturena side has prioritised strategic deals.

Thabo Moloisane, as cited by the Kaizer Chiefs website, arrived from Stellenbosch FC earlier this year.

The 27-year-old defender made 64 appearances for Stellies.



For Kaizer Chiefs, their first signing of the transfer window was a signal of intent.

The team had been criticised for a lack of experience in the backline, with Moloisane expected to shore up the defence.

Chiefs backed up his signing by adding Khanyisa Mayo, a proven finisher.



The forward was on loan from CR Belouizdad in Algeria before the Amakhosi decided to make the move permanent.

Chiefs also signed Tanzanian midfielder Adolf Bitegeko and goalkeeper Renaldo Leaner to improve their squad depth.

Chiefs announce signing of Mtasingwa from Tanzania



Kaizer Chiefs have secured the services of Adolf Mtasingwa Bitegeko from Tanzanian giants, Azam FC for an undisclosed fee, following successful negotiations between the two Clubs.



The 27-year-old defensive midfielder, who was… pic.twitter.com/OQ4pmVZGWp  July 21, 2026

Loser: Mamelodi Sundowns

On paper, the club appears to have lost more than it has gained.

Among the high-profile departures for Mamelodi Sundowns is Peter Shalulile, as reported by ESPN Africa.

The veteran striker fell out of favour under coach Miguel Cardoso, despite his contributions over six years.



Winger Thapelo Maseko also departed Sundowns in August to join Danish giants FC Copenhagen, while midfielder Miguel Reisinho also left to become a free agent.

The CAF Champions League title-holders have made five signings in this window.

These include Antonio van Wyk, Siyanda Ndlovu, Tsiki Ntsabaleng, and Cassius Mailula.



Perhaps the biggest signing for Sundowns is Deano van Rooyen, trading Orlando Pirates for Chloorkop.

While these players may have first-team impact, it could be argued that the club has downgraded in terms of reputation.

Cardoso has also spoken openly about team stability, believing things will improve once the transfer market closes on 22 September.



Presenting our new South African lion…. Thapelo Maseko 🇿🇦🦁#fcklive pic.twitter.com/cgb68MPdrb — F.C. København (@FCKobenhavn) August 18, 2026

Winner: Orlando Pirates

The PSL champions have been the talk of this transfer window, making 10 signings.

Norwegian striker Sebastian Pedersen is among the biggest moves, alongside several experienced local players to add depth.



Among these names are Thapelo Mokobodi, Mthetheleli Mthiyane, Sbangani Zulu, and Neo Rapoo, scouted from other PSL clubs.

It is worth noting that Orlando Pirates’ transfer activity was mostly necessary due to injuries and some big-name departures.

The biggest loss for the Buccaneers was Relebohile Mofokeng joining Belgian side Royale Union Saint-Gilloise in July.



As cited by Times Live, coach Abdeslam Ouaddou admitted that Pirates needed to fill the gap left by the forward’s departure.

“[Mofokeng] was an important player for the club. If you can just see his data, his involvement in chance creation was huge, but I believe it’s important to find a profile that can take the baton.”

Loser: Stellenbosch FC

With the loss of Moloisane to Chiefs and Mthiyane to Pirates, among others, the club may be the hardest hit by the transfer market.



Stellenbosch FC coach Gavin Hunt has even spoken on record about the intense window.

“I’ve never seen such player movement in the PSL with every club,” he reacted, as cited by BusinessDay.

He estimated that around 20 players had departed Stellies and believes club budgets are to blame.



Either way, losing several players to direct rivals is a major threat for the club.

With the club in 11th on the PSL table, transfer market losses will make things even more complicated for Stellenbosch.

World.title: Anele Tembe inquest: Eyewitness details gruesome discovery
World.content:
Eyewitness Rob Stefanutto details what happened on the morning Anele Tembe fell to her death. Images via IG

Rob Steffanutto – the man who reportedly saw AKA, real name Kiernan Forbes, moments after Anele Tembe’s fatal fall off the 10th-floor balcony of the Pepperclub Hotel, and helped her in her dying moments – has shared details of his gruesome discovery on day one of her inquest, heard at the Cape Town Magistrates Court.

The formal hearing, which is not a criminal trial, will take place over the next few days.

Thus far, six witnesses have already testified – two police officers, a hotel manager and employee, and two witnesses, one of whom had video footage.



ANELE INQUEST: EYEWITNESS DETAILS GRUESOME DISCOVERY

Addressing the court, Cape Town businessman Rob Stefanutto detailed the sequence of events from before Anele Tembe’s fatal fall to his comforting her in her dying moments.

The property agent had been staying at The Sentinel hotel, which ran parallel to The Pepperlub Hotel on Loop Street.

His balcony was on the same eye level as the one belonging to AKA and Anele’s room, a mere 50-60 metres away.



Around 7.30 am on the morning of 11 April 2021, Rob recalled hearing a fight between a man and a woman. The woman – Anele Tembe- repeatedly shouted the words: “Leave me alone, get away from me”.

Shortly afterwards, he heard what he described as a wailing sound, followed by a loud bang. He then heard a man – AKA – shout the words: “My God, my God”.

From his hotel balcony, Rob saw the body of Anele lying on the pavement below. He also saw AKA standing on his hotel room balcony.



He immediately rushed down to the ground floor, where he discovered Anele’s naked body covered with a sheet, which was placed over her by a hotel employee.

Anele Tembe fell to her death off the 10th floor of the Pepperclub Hotel in 2021.

COMFORTING ANELE TEMBE IN HER DYING MOMENTS

Rob Stefanutto continued his testimony in the inquest that he had discovered that Anele Tembe was still alive, despite falling 10 floors to the ground.

He told the court, “I pulled the sheet back, and she was alive. Her eyes were open. I saw a young black woman who had blood coming out of her mouth. She was completely naked under it.



“Her left leg was broken. I said to her, ‘If you can’t speak, blink,’ and she blinked.”

Rob administered CPR to Anele and wiped blood off her face. He comforted her and told her not to be afraid, as help, via the paramedics, was on the way.

He continued: “I just sort of prayed to her. I didn’t know if she was a religious person, and that seemed to calm and comfort her.”



Paramedics eventually arrived and attempted to resuscitate Anele after she went into cardiac arrest. However, her injuries were too severe, and Anele was declared deceased on the scene.

AKA ‘CHOSE TO HIDE’

Between the time of Anele Tembe’s fall and her death, her fiancé AKA remained in his hotel room.

He later revealed his entourage had told him not to go down to the pavement where Anele lay dying.



Admonishing AKA for his no-show, Rob Stefanutto was quoted in the book When Live Kills: The Tragic Tale of AKA and Anele as saying, “If someone jumps off a building and you are their fiancé, you come downstairs. One has to wonder whether he didnt come down and instead chose to hide away upstairs because he might have been scared that I would recognise him. He had seen me standing on the balcony across his room just after she dropped”.

Rob then made a surprising comment about what happened thereafter.

He continued: “After all this happened, I went to the senior police officer, and I said that I’d like to make a statement. And then I waited and waited, but no one ever contacted me”.



A few days later, Rob received a call from Moses Tembe’s attorney, who helped him submit a detailed statement about the incident.

Rob then hinted at foul play.

He continued: “It was submitted to the authorities…but to this day, I don’t know what happened to that statement.

World.title: Orlando Pirates news: Ouaddou to collect huge debt, Appollis price tag revealed?
World.content:
Today’s Orlando Pirates news wrap looks at a huge price tag for Oswin Appollis. There’s also a massive debt owed to manager Abdeslam Ouaddou.

Ouaddou must collect a debt from his old club

Abdeslam Ouaddou is awaiting a multi-million-rand claim from old club AS Vita, a club he coached briefly in 2024.

Appollis could leave after Nkota’s arrival at Orlando Pirates

An unnamed club has tabled an enticing offer for Bafana Bafana winger Oswin Appollis, and Pirates are considering it. The 25-year-old featured in every single Betway Premiership match last season for the champions, contributing nine goals and six assists in 30 outings. This term, he’s already got two goals and two assists in five matches. The transfer window closes on 21 September. Rumours suggest it will take a massive fee to convince Pirates to sell.



Midfield improvisation

Meanwhile, in the continued absence of injured midfield duo Sihle Nduli and Thalente Mbatha, Cemran Dansin, Thapelo Mokobodi, Simphiwe Selepe and Mthiyane have all gotten plenty of minutes in the Bucs engine room. They might be needed for longer than planned. What looked like a crisis on paper has proved to be a massive opportunity for some of the club’s emerging stars. Next up for Pirates is a CAF Champions League qualifying second-leg clash with La Cure Waves on Saturday 12 September. The sides drew 0-0 in the first leg on Sunday. The champions’ next league match is on Thursday, 17 September against Durban City. Reminder of the XI which started against La Cure Waves:

Chaine; Zulu, Derbyshire, Seema, Hotto; Selepe, Mthiyane, Dansin; Appollis, Radiopane; Msendami.

Unique run of domestic results for Orlando Pirates

The Sea Robbers have made a superb start to their title defence, winning four of five matches and drawing the other. Title rivals Sundowns have an identical record so far. After four consecutive domestic wins with 1-0, 2-0, 3-0 and 4-0 scorelines, the champions have done something that no other Betway Premiership side has done in history. The sequence started with a 1-0 win over Sekhukhune in the MTN8 and continued with successes over Sekhukhune in the league, Sekhukhune again in the MTN8 semi-final second leg, and a 4-0 trouncing of Kruger United.

World.title: Weather Report: fine in the west, cloudy and cool everywhere else
World.content:
Fine conditions in the west contrast with cloudy, cool weather elsewhere on Tuesday: Image ChatGPT

Tuesday, 8 September’s Weather Report shows fine conditions in places in the west, while the rest of the country stays cloudy and cold to cool with isolated to scattered showers and thundershowers.

SAWS confirms no severe weather warnings are active today.

Gauteng can expect cloudy and cool weather with isolated showers and rain. A “high” UVB sunburn index is in effect, so sun precautions are worth taking if you’re outdoors for long.



REMEMBER | Weather Report: a milder Monday after a wet, wild weekend

according to SAWS, most of the country stays cloudy and cool today

Mpumalanga sees morning fog patches along the escarpment, otherwise cloudy and cool to cold with isolated showers and rain.

Limpopo starts with morning fog patches along the escarpment too, otherwise cloudy and cool with isolated showers and rain.

North West stays cloudy and cool, becoming partly cloudy in the afternoon, with isolated showers and rain in the east.

The Free State sees morning fog patches in the extreme east, otherwise cloudy to partly cloudy with isolated showers and rain, except in the west.

The Northern Cape stays cloudy with morning fog along the coast, otherwise partly cloudy, windy and cool to warm, but fine and hot in the west.



The Western Cape sees partly cloudy conditions over the north-eastern parts, otherwise fine and warm to hot. The UVB sunburn index here is “very high” today.

The western half of the Eastern Cape stays fine and warm. The eastern half starts with morning fog in places before turning fine and warm, cool in the north.

KwaZulu-Natal sees morning fog over the interior, otherwise partly cloudy and cool to warm with isolated showers and rain in the north. The UVB sunburn index is “high” here too.

why the west is staying dry while everywhere else stays cloudy

This split in conditions is tied to the cut-off low that’s dominated the country’s weather for over a week.

According to SAWS, the system is beginning to weaken, though it remains active enough to keep producing showers and thundershowers over the eastern interior, even as its influence on the Western Cape fades.

It’s genuinely striking to see such a clean divide between fine and hot conditions in the west and cloudy, cool weather everywhere else. A good reminder that even a weakening system can still leave its mark.

World.title: Biko inquest: Former Security Branch officer denies covering up torture
World.content:
GQBERHA - Security Branch police were infamous for using excessive force and torture to intimidate those who opposed apartheid.

But decades later, some former officers who acted on behalf of the apartheid state continue to deny wrongdoing.

Former Captain Daniel Siebert is one of them.

He is being cross-examined at the inquest into the murder of Black Consciousness Movement leader Steve Biko.

Siebert told the inquest that part of his duties was to quell tensions allegedly fuelled by anti-apartheid activists.

Such activism was viewed by the apartheid state as a declaration of war.

Biko was among those targeted by the Security Branch, and the circumstances surrounding his death are still being investigated almost five decades later.

The State alleges that Siebert and other officers tortured Biko in the days before his death.

It disputes the former officers’ account that Biko was fatally injured during a scuffle with police.

The inquest is expected to hear from another person of interest, as well as former Security Branch policeman Jacobus Beneke and ex-apartheid spy Craig Williamson, who are expected to be called as the next witnesses.

World.title: From hospital threat to gunfire: Key evidence in Matlala trial
World.content:
PRETORIA - Security threats, gunfire and disputed bail evidence have emerged in the trial within a trial in the attempted murder case against alleged criminal kingpin Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala and his co-accused.

Three witnesses took the stand as alleged hitman Musa Kekana continues challenging the admissibility of evidence obtained during his arrest.

Kekana claims police assaulted him during his arrest, saying he was beaten until he began coughing up blood.

Proceedings began with former Bramley Police Station commander Owen King in the witness box.

He testified that while Kekana was receiving treatment at Edenvale Hospital, police received intelligence about an imminent threat.

The court then heard from an eyewitness who was detained alongside Kekana on the day of his arrest.

He testified that Kekana had called him to request a vehicle rim. When Kekana arrived to collect it, gunfire suddenly broke out.

During cross-examination, the eyewitness described the police’s behaviour on the day as aggressive.

The State also wants to introduce evidence from Kekana’s failed bail application.

The defence has objected, arguing that Kekana was not properly warned that statements made during the bail proceedings could later be used against him at trial.

Judge Cassim Moosa is expected to rule on the admissibility of that evidence on Tuesday.

World.title: LIVESTREAM | Mapisa-Nqakula back in witness box as corruption trial continues
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Former Defence Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula is back on the witness stand as her corruption and money-laundering trial continues in the Gauteng High Court in Pretoria.

On Monday, the court dismissed her application to have the charges against her withdrawn.

Mapisa-Nqakula faces 12 counts of corruption and one count of money laundering, stemming from allegations that she solicited and received millions of rand in bribes while serving as Defence Minister.

She took the stand on Monday to give her version of events and denied allegations that she agreed with defence contractor Nombasa Ntsondwa-Ndhlovu to use coded language to conceal alleged bribe payments.

However, Mapisa-Nqakula has acknowledged meeting the State’s key witness three times in 2017.

She maintains that the meetings were purely social and insists that money was never discussed.

World.title: Praying for rain as fires, haze plague Indonesian Borneo
World.content:
Hundreds of schools have been closed indefinitely in West Kalimantan due to air pollution, with about 200,000 pupils learning from home, according to the provincial education ministry.

The kids are being kept home for their health, Syarifah told AFP in a classroom empty but for two teachers presenting classes online, both with dozens of pupils scattered across their screens.

"The hope is that at home, in terms of health, they can be protected... because they are inside the house. They don't have to go through roads full of dust and smoke," she said.

But Syarifah said not every child has stable internet or access to a computer, making live sessions difficult for some.

"Sometimes... there is a power outage at their home, or they forget to charge their phones", and some students live in faraway areas with patchy connectivity, she said.

The school's teachers have been showing up every day as usual, giving lessons online in classrooms with no air purifiers. They work maskless so students can understand them clearly.

Syarifah said the school would offer extra lessons for free once in-person learning resumes.

"We hope that this haze will pass quickly. Usually after the rain falls, the haze will disappear," she said.

West Kalimantan's wetter season usually starts around October or November.

- The health official -

Iwansyah, head of the Kubu Raya regency's health agency, is responsible for the welfare of some 700,000 people spread over 123 villages, served by one general hospital and 21 clinics.

His staff focus on efforts to prevent illness caused by "the unhealthy air people inhale every day".

World.title: Eiffel Tower closed in row over women removed for Hindu group
World.content:
PARIS - The Eiffel Tower was closed on Monday because of a strike by staff over the removal of female colleagues during a visit by a Hindu religious group, workers and management said.

The visit came on the same day as a cultural boat procession on the Seine organised by the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) spiritual movement.

In a statement, Eiffel Tower staff condemned "professional instructions that led to female employees being sidelined, replaced and made invisible because of their sex" during the visit by the delegation.

"Instructions were given to female employees of the Eiffel Tower and to female employees of contractors to make themselves invisible in order to welcome this delegation," the staff said in their statement, adding they were shocked to have been put in such a situation.

"Some were asked to leave their posts and withdraw to other areas. In some posts they were replaced by men. And all female employees were instructed not to go through or cross certain areas while the delegation was present."

The operating company that runs the Paris landmark, SETE, acknowledged that the Hindu delegation had requested the visit be organised so as to limit "interactions with women" and said that "these conditions should not have been accepted".

The conditions "were not in line with SETE's values, nor with the principles of equality between men and women," the company said, promising to accept the "consequences".

"It is clearly not an acceptable practice," SETE president Ariel Weil, who is also a socialist elected official in Paris, told AFP.

"I restate the Eiffel Tower's commitment to republican values and to the equality of men and women."

The French capital's socialist mayor Emmanuel Gregoire said on X it was "unacceptable" that the Tower management agreed to the delegation's conditions, and said an investigation would be launched.

- Hindu nationalist ties -

The Tower, which receives nearly seven million visitors a year according to its website, was closed all day on Monday, but will open as normal on Tuesday according to a staff representative.

BAPS, which is close to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling conservative Hindu nationalist party, consecrated its first major temple in France on Sunday, near Paris.

French Equality Minister Aurore Berge reacted angrily on X.

"In France, we do not ask women to erase themselves. No dogma, no religion is above the laws of the Republic," she wrote.

Far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen also criticised the incident, saying France would "never accept that women's presence be 'limited'".

Gabriel Attal, a centrist rival to become president, said that "in France, no culture, no belief, no religion, nothing and no one can come and dictate to women what their place should be".

World.title: Maresca agrees with Haaland that players started season jaded
World.content:
LONDON - Manchester City coach Enzo Maresca said finding form early in the season "was not easy" for his World Cup players ahead of the club's Champions League opener at Porto.

"I think it's correct that you see these kind of players that they start to be tired," Maresca said at the Dragao Stadium before Tuesday's match.

Maresca was responding to remarks by Erling Haaland posted on the striker's his YouTube channel earlier in the day.

The Norwegian has three goals in three league matches but did not play in warm-up games, following Norway's run to the World Cup quarterfinals.

"The new season started and I didn't even have a pre-season. I normally have a bit of pre-season but this time, just nothing," said Haaland.

"The physical side will come, if you manage to stay injury-free, but you need to be sharp mentally as well, and that's not easy.

"We need to have that eager feeling to go back but we don't because there is no time to properly stay away from football because there are so many games and the season is longer.

"I'm not complaining because it's still a positive thing that you get to play football throughout the whole year and live off it.

"But sometimes we need a break as well.

"I never played a World Cup so I don't know how it is."

Maresca was sympathetic.

"It's it's not easy for them it's not easy for Erling, it's not easy for most of the players that they continue to play for their international team," said the coach.

"It's correct to give them some rest that can be one game out or can be one week away depends a little bit in which moment we are.

"To be focused on the day by day makes it very complicated to think where we can be in February, March, April in terms of expectations.

"The most important thing is to see that we are improving game after game."

World.title: Jakarta airport and others reopen after volcanic ash crisis
World.content:
JAKARTA - Indonesia's main airport and several other air travel hubs reopened early Tuesday after days of closure due to ash from a volcanic eruption, the Transport Ministry said.

The ministry wrote on Instagram that the airport serving the capital Jakarta and four others near the city or around the island of Java are now operating again, as the air safety crisis that left hundreds of thousands of travellers stranded subsides.

Mount Anak Krakatau, about 150 kilometres from Jakarta, erupted on Saturday, spewing a fountain of lava and a plume of volcanic ash.

Eight airports halted operations over the weekend after ash was detected in their airspace, disrupting nearly 3,000 flights and leaving more than 340,000 passengers stranded, the Transport Ministry reported on Monday.

Early Tuesday the ministry posted on Instagram that Jakarta's airport and four others are up and running again.

Jakarta's main airport wrote on Instagram that "following the current volcanic eruption activity of Mount Anak Krakatau, Soekarno-Hatta International Airport has resumed flight operations."

Earlier, the airport closures had been repeatedly extended.

Airlines now face the daunting task of getting all the stranded passengers onto planes and to their intended destinations after days of chaos at the airports.

The other four listed as reopening include Halim Perdanakusuma, a smaller Jakarta-area airport that caters to both civil and military flights, and Hussein Sastranegara in Bandung, the capital of West Java, the Transport Ministry said.

Another small airport in south Sumatra resumed operations on Monday morning. So two of the original eight are still closed.

More than 240 domestic and international flights were cancelled or delayed due to volcanic ash on Monday morning alone, Soekarno-Hatta airport said, adding that nearly 30,000 passengers were affected.

The Transport Ministry had prepared six alternative airports as options for aircraft that were originally scheduled to land in Jakarta.

Anak Krakatau, which means Child of Krakatau, sits in a strait that separates the islands of Java and Sumatra.

The volcano has been sporadically active since it emerged from the sea at the beginning of last century in the caldera that formed after the 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatau.

A 2018 tsunami triggered by a collapse of parts of Anak Krakatau killed 429 people and displaced thousands.

World.title: SA's drug problem: Why international cartels are moving in
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa is increasingly becoming an attractive base for international drug syndicates, according to security expert Willem Els of the Institute for Security Studies.

Els says Mexican drug cartels are allegedly sending experienced drug cooks to South Africa to operate industrial-scale laboratories, while working with established local criminal networks to manufacture and distribute drugs.

On Monday, a 45-year-old man was arrested at OR Tambo International Airport after police allegedly found cocaine worth more than R800,000 in his luggage.

The arrest comes amid growing concerns over the emergence of large-scale drug laboratories in South Africa.

Three suspected crystal meth laboratories have been uncovered in less than four months.

In May, police raided a remote farm northwest of Johannesburg, uncovering what they described as a multi-million-dollar methamphetamine laboratory.

Eleven suspects were arrested, including four Mexican nationals who police suspected of having links to Latin American drug cartels.

Then, in August, another crystal meth laboratory was uncovered near the Zimbabwean border, with several foreign nationals, including two Mexicans, arrested.

Earlier this month, a laboratory was uncovered during a raid on a farm about 200 kilometres north of Johannesburg.

“That is very concerning that we see that these international cartels are having a presence more and more in South Africa.”

According to Els, there is no clear indication that Mexican cartels have simply transplanted their entire operations to South Africa. Instead, they are allegedly forming links with criminal networks that already operate in the country.

These local connections can provide access to established markets, trafficking routes and distribution networks, making it easier for international syndicates to manufacture drugs locally and move them across borders.

“It is concerning. If you look at the quantities that have been discovered, it means that our market must be very big or we’ve got a very lucrative export market.”

World.title: Ruto signs law targeting officials who ignore audit findings
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto sign into law four Bills at State House on September 8, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has signed into law changes that could penalise public entities for failing to implement recommendations by the Auditor-General and Controller of Budget.

The Public Finance Management Amendment Bill 2025 is one of four Bills Ruto assented to, alongside legislation on population planning, air passenger charges and trust administration.

The amendments shorten the period within which public entities must submit financial statements and introduce penalties for failing to implement recommendations arising from reports by the Auditor-General and Controller of Budget, including findings adopted by Parliament or county assemblies.

The changes seek to strengthen oversight of public funds and ensure recommendations by constitutional oversight institutions are acted on.

Ruto also signed the National Council for Population and Development Bill, which establishes the National Council for Population and Development as a statutory body responsible for population and development matters.

The council will coordinate population policies and programmes, support evidence-based population planning and advise the Government on population growth, demographic trends and their impact on economic and social development.

The President noted that the legislation comes as Kenya shapes its development agenda beyond Vision 2030.

The Air Passenger Service Charge Amendment Bill also became law, changing the framework for collecting and administering charges paid by air passengers.

The amendments provide a legal basis for additional institutions to benefit from the proceeds, including the Kenya Airports Authority, Kenya Civil Aviation Authority, Kenya Meteorological Department and Tourism Fund.

The changes are intended to support aviation infrastructure, regulation, weather services and tourism while providing a clearer framework for managing passenger service charge revenue.

The fourth legislation, the Trust Administration Bill, creates a single legal framework for administering trusts.

The law repeals the Trustees (Perpetual Succession) Act and the Trustee Act, replacing them with one principal statute.

The Government expects the new framework to remove duplication and inconsistencies in trust law while making it easier for trustees and beneficiaries to understand and administer trusts.

The legislation will also provide a framework for trusts used in estate planning, asset management and administration of property on behalf of beneficiaries.

World.title: Centum taps insider as Mworia exits after nearly two decades
World.content:
Centum Investment Company PLC acting Group Chief Executive Thomas Omondi-Achola. [Courtesy]

Centum Investment Company PLC has appointed Thomas Omondi-Achola as acting group chief executive, tapping an internal candidate to succeed long-serving CEO James Mworia, who is leaving to head Kenya’s newly established National Infrastructure Fund (NIF).

The transition, effective immediately, marks the end of an 18-year tenure during which Mworia transformed Centum from a small investment firm into East Africa’s largest diversified investment platform, the company said in a statement.

World.title: Ruto: Kenya to end raw mineral exports
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during a thanksgiving service in South Horr, Samburu County on September 6, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto says Kenya will no longer allow its mineral wealth to leave the country in raw form, coming days after the controversial saga surrounding Tata Chemicals’ operations at Lake Magadi.

Ruto defended the government’s decision to suspend Tata Chemicals’ operations at Lake Magadi, Kajiado County, arguing that Kenya has not been receiving sufficient value from the natural resource and that more investors should be given an opportunity to develop the area.

“We want to give five, six or even 10 companies an opportunity to use the resources there to create jobs, value, create wealth and reduce poverty,” Ruto said.

The President made the remarks during a thanksgiving service in South Horr, Samburu County, on Sunday, where he announced a broader government policy aimed at shifting Kenya from exporting raw materials to processing them locally.

“Going into the future, our position as the government. Whether we are talking about Magadi Soda or oil or all our minerals, we have taken the decision that we will no longer export raw materials,” Ruto said.

“We are going to process all minerals available in Kenya.”

The declaration puts the long-running Lake Magadi dispute at the centre of a much wider economic strategy.

Tata Chemicals has been associated with soda ash production at the lake for more than a century. Its Kenyan operations trace their history to 1911, when the Magadi Soda Company began extracting trona from Lake Magadi.

Operations were suspended on July 28, 2026, following a directive from the Ministry of Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs over compliance and licensing issues.

Ruto has argued that the resource should generate greater benefits for Kenyans through expanded investment, job creation and local value addition.

He accused the existing model of allowing valuable resources to leave the country while Kenya receives less economic benefit than it could.

The President’s comments reflect a longstanding challenge facing Kenya’s extractive sector: how to turn mineral deposits into manufacturing opportunities rather than simply exporting commodities.

Under the proposed approach, minerals such as gold, limestone, iron ore, graphite, titanium and soda ash would be processed or refined in Kenya before being exported.

The government says this would create industrial jobs, strengthen local supply chains and increase the value of exports.

Ruto cited planned cooperation with Nigerian businessman Aliko Dangote as an example of the investment model the government wants to pursue.

He said talks were underway to establish an oil refinery and petrochemical complex in Lamu, alongside efforts to attract investors into mineral refining.

“It is imprudent for any government to export raw materials, create jobs and value in other countries while we have a big population of young people who need jobs,” Ruto said.

World.title: Sifuna condemns abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Busia County Senator Okiya Omtata, Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, Bumula MP Jack Wamboka during the burial service of Mary Gorreti Okiya at Kabula, in Bumula on September 5,2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna has declared that the fight to restore democracy, media freedom and the rule of law following the abduction of Standard Group Senior Editor will form the centrepiece of the Linda Mwananchi government vowing to defeat President William Ruto in the 2027 General Election.

Sifuna accused President Ruto’s administration of undermining constitutional freedoms and creating an atmosphere of fear, saying the country must be returned to what he described as “the rail of the six important values” enshrined in the Constitution.

Speaking in Bumula Constituency, Kakamega County during the burial of Mary Goreti, the sister of Busia Senator Okiya Omtatah, Sifuna strongly condemned the abduction and arrest of a Standard Group Associate Editor, Alex Kiprotich, arguing that journalists must be protected if Kenya is to remain a democratic country.

“It is impossible that you are driving on the road and you are taken away the way the way the Standard Group Journaliat and Editor Alex Kiprotich was taken. Kenyans want to live in a free country. We do not want to live in fear,” said Sifuna.

He questioned the circumstances surrounding the incident and accused the Government of failing to protect media freedom, adding that the Linda Mwananchi movement would seek to restore institutions and constitutional safeguards if elected to power, arguing that democracy could not survive where citizens, journalists and political opponents lived in fear.

"You cannot just arrest a senior journalist in the middle of the road with police carrying firearms, then you dump him some 500kilometres near the dam, a country cannot have democracy if media is not being respected and allowed to do it's work as per the constitution," said Sifuna.

He said the movement’s agenda was not merely about removing the current administration from power but it's main plan is rebuilding systems of governance around constitutionalism, democracy, individual freedoms and the rule of law.

“With less than 11 months remaining, we want to tell Kenyans that our entire plan is to return this country to the rails of the six important values contained in our Constitution, including democracy, freedom of citizens and the rule of law,” said Sifuna.

Sifuna also accused the Government of using threats against political opponents, saying leaders should not threaten citizens with arrest, expulsion or other forms of intimidation.

He challenged religious leaders to remind politicians that the power to determine the length of a person's life belongs to God.

Sifuna further linked the rule of law to economic growth, warning that investors would be reluctant to establish businesses in Kenya if government could arbitrarily order them to leave.

He said Kenya could not rely on government alone to create employment for millions of young people, arguing that the country needed both local and foreign investors.

“No investor can bring his project to a country where he can wake up one day and the President tells him, ‘Pack and go.’ It is impossible,” Sifuna said.

He argued that investor confidence was also affected by the possibility of commercial disputes being referred to foreign jurisdictions because investors lacked confidence in Kenya’s legal system.

Sifuna also criticised the government over the ongoing nurses and midwives strike, saying the rule of law required the State to honour agreements signed with workers.

World.title: Murkomen reaffirms IG Kanja's command of National Police Service
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has reaffirmed that the Inspector General of Police retains constitutional command of the National Police Service, saying the government will continue to respect the independence of the office.

Speaking during the passing-out parade of new Administration Police recruits in Nairobi, Murkomen said the Inspector General has authority over key operational matters within the service, including investigations, promotions and deployment of officers.

“Your Excellency, the Inspector General of Police retains the command of the National Police Service, especially on matters of investigation, promotion and deployment of officers without interference from anyone, including the Cabinet Secretary. We will continue respecting Article 245 of the Constitution,” Murkomen said.

His remarks come amid public debate over the relationship between the Interior Ministry and the National Police Service, particularly allegations that political leaders sometimes issue direct instructions to police officers.

Murkomen dismissed criticism directed at the office of the Inspector General, describing some of its proponents as tribalists and propagandists. He maintained that the Inspector General is carrying out his responsibilities and said he had confidence in the leadership of the police service.

“I have full faith in the IG and believe that every act that is done by the National Police Service is guided by the Constitution,” he said.

The Cabinet Secretary also addressed concerns over his role in directing the police, saying that his responsibility is primarily to provide policy direction rather than interfere with the operational command of the service.

“When required to give policy direction, I always give it in writing and we will continue to support the independence of the National Police Service from external interference,” Murkomen said.

During the ceremony, Murkomen also cautioned the newly graduated officers against corruption, excessive alcohol consumption and conduct that could undermine the reputation of the police service.

He urged the recruits to uphold discipline and protect the dignity of the police uniform, noting that the respect they receive from members of the public would depend largely on their conduct.

The Cabinet Secretary encouraged the officers to understand the responsibility that comes with joining the National Police Service and to discharge their duties within the confines of the Constitution and the law.

The passing-out ceremony marked the entry of the new recruits into the police service that made the CS use the occasion to emphasize professional conduct and respect for the constitutional framework governing policing in Kenya.

World.title: Ruto assures Kajiado residents of full control of Amboseli National Park
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto inspects the Rombo Clusters Irrigation Development Project in Kajiado County on September 3, 2026. [Peterson Githaiga, Standard]

President William Ruto has assured Kajiado residents that they will soon have full control of the management of Amboseli National Park, following his decision to return the park to the county in November 2025.

However, he said the transfer has been temporarily halted by the court.

The President hit out at those he accused of frustrating the move, saying they will be in for a rude shock.

“They took us to court over the Social Health Authority and the Affordable Housing Programme, but these programmes are progressing well. Similarly, I want to assure the people of Kajiado that, before the end of this year, Amboseli will be fully in the hands of Kajiado County,” he said.

Speaking in Kajiado County on Thursday during his development tour, President Ruto reiterated that he will not relent in his pursuit of equity and inclusive development across Kenya, saying that longstanding inequalities have unduly benefited certain regions at the expense of others.

He revealed that the securitisation of the Road Maintenance Levy Fund and the Sports Fund has enabled the Government to clear pending bills in the roads sector and construct 6,000km of new roads, and accelerate the construction of 32 new stadia across the country.

"The Road Maintenance Levy Fund was misused to only build roads in some parts of the country. Those opposing securitisation are unhappy that we are advancing equity," he said.

The President began his tour at Oloirien in Kajiado South Constituency by inspecting progress of the 67km Illasit-Rombo-Chala-Njukini-Taveta road, which is 48 per cent completed.

The Sh9.4 billion project will cut travel time between Kajiado and Taita-Taveta counties from two hours to just 40 minutes, thus easing the movement of goods and people.

The Head of State announced that eight new roads of 220km are being built across Kajiado County at a cost of Sh13 billion to open up the region and improve transport.

The President commissioned Sh221 million Rombo Clusters Irrigation Development Project, which is expected to enhance livelihoods and boost irrigation in the area.

He also inspected progress of the Sh2.2 billion Loitoktok Affordable Housing Project, and laid the foundation stone for the Sh220 million Loitoktok Kenya Medical Training College student hostels with a 580-bed capacity.

At Kimana, in Kajiado South Constituency, President Ruto commissioned the Sh2.7 billion Sultan Hamud-Loitoktok 132kV Transmission Line and Loitoktok Sub-Station, which will serve the residents of Kajiado South and parts of Makueni County.

He inspected construction of the Kimana modern market, which is aimed at giving traders dignified working environment.

At Namanga, Kajiado Central Constituency, the President commissioned the Namanga Sub-Station, a project of the Kenya Electricity Transmission Company (KETRACO), which is part of the 132KV Machakos- Konza-Isinya-Namanga Transmission Project.

Namanga Modern Market, which is under construction at a cost of Sh50 million, will benefit 120 traders at the border town.

In Kajiado town, the President toured the construction of the Kajiado Affordable Housing Project, a Sh473 million investment that will deliver 196 housing units, as well as the 100-unit police housing project at a cost of Sh137 million.

He also inspected the progress of the 580-bed student hostels at Maasai National Polytechnic, which is being built at a cost of KSh216 million.

Ruto ordered the closer of Tata Chemicals, saying the government will identify a new and responsible investor to take over soda ash mining operations at Lake Magadi.

The President said Tata Chemicals had failed to adequately modernise the plant, create sufficient employment opportunities for residents, and deliver meaningful economic benefits to the people of Kenya.

“It is unfair for one company to dominate the ownership and operations of Magadi Soda for years, yet it has done little to improve the factory or create employment opportunities for our youth,” he said at Rombo in Kajiado South Constituency.

He added: “Because they have been unable to do anything meaningful with the plant for more than 100 years, I have directed them to pack up and go.”

The Ministry of Mining suspended the company’s mining operations in July 2026 over concerns relating to regulatory compliance, value addition and licensing.

The ministry also ordered the closure of the company’s depot in Kajiado Town for contravening environmental regulations.

In addition, the company has been unable to reach an agreement with the Kajiado County Government over a land rates dispute following the expiry of its operating licence in 2023.

The plant produces soda ash, or sodium carbonate, a key industrial mineral used in the manufacture of glass, soap and laundry detergents, among other products.

Despite being Africa’s largest soda ash producer, President Ruto noted that the operation had not delivered commensurate benefits to Kenyans over its more than 100-year history, particularly because much of the soda ash produced is exported for processing and consumption in overseas markets.

The Government, the President said, would therefore prioritise an investor capable of modernising the facility, expanding local value addition, creating jobs for young people, and ensuring that Kenya derives greater economic value from its natural resources.

World.title: IG Kanja orders probe into abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Standard Group PLC Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja has ordered immediate and transparent investigations into the alleged abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich in Gilgil.

The National Police Service (NPS) said it had taken note of reports that Kiprotich was allegedly kidnapped on Tuesday and had moved swiftly to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

NPS spokesperson Muchiri Nyaga said the police service treats kidnapping and abduction with the utmost seriousness, describing the offences as a threat to the lives, liberty and security of Kenyans.

“The Inspector General of Police has accordingly ordered immediate investigations to determine what transpired, including the identity of the heavily armed individuals reportedly seen ordering occupants out of their vehicle,” Nyaga said in a statement.

The NPS said its Anti-Abduction Unit, established to investigate abductions and disappearances, had taken up the matter and would work to ensure that those responsible are brought to justice.

“We unequivocally condemn any act of kidnapping, abduction, or intimidation intended to interfere with press freedom or any other constitutional right,” Nyaga said.

The police service assured the public that the investigation into the Gilgil incident would be conducted transparently, stressing that no one was above the law.

The development comes amid growing condemnation of Kiprotich’s alleged abduction, with the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) also calling for an immediate investigation.

CPJ Africa Director Angela Quintal described the incident as a “shameful indictment” of the Kenya Kwanza administration, raising concerns over the safety of journalists and press freedom in the country.

“The attempt to forcibly disappear Alex Kiprotich, three days after President William Ruto railed against The Standard Group, reflects the growing dangers that journalists face in Kenya, despite the president’s earlier promise to allow the press to work freely,” Quintal said.

The New York-based press freedom organisation further expressed concern over what it described as an escalation in cases of abductions and enforced disappearances in Kenya.

World.title: Trumpets of reforms blow louder as Kenya marks 16 years under 2010 Constitution
World.content:
The Constitution, Kenyan flag and the National anthem. [PCS]

On Thursday, August 27, a group of people largely composed of the youth gathered under some trees at Jeevanjee Gardens in Nairobi, carrying Kenyans flag, and banners and placards inscribed with "implement the constitution. Kenyans first" words.

These were in protests against what they believed is deliberate failure of those in authority to fully implement the 2010 Constitution.

World.title: Russia pounds Kyiv one day after visit by Witkoff and Kushner
World.content:
Kyiv —

Russia pounded Ukraine’s capital Kyiv with missiles and drones on Tuesday morning, killing two people, one day after US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited the region in an attempt to kickstart stalled peace talks.

Explosions rang out in the city early Tuesday local time, according to a CNN reporter in Kyiv, in a signal the agreed three day-halt on attacks as Washington’s emissaries visited both country’s capitals was over.

Two people were killed and 10 were wounded in the attack, which involved ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as drones.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the assault was “complex” and designed by Russia to “cause as much harm to life as possible.”

The attack caused “significant damage to residential buildings and other civilian infrastructure in the capital,” Zelensky said on X.

People were rescued after being trapped in a five-story residential block damaged in the onslaught in Kyiv’s Solomyanskyi district, emergency services said. A warehouse and garages in other districts were also damaged and images from officials showed cars on fire.

Kyiv’s mayor Vitali Klitschko said an educational institution had been damaged.

This photograph shows smoke rising following Russian missiles strike in Kyiv, Ukraine, on September 8, 2026. Eugene Kotenko/AFP/Getty Images

The attacks also struck a civilian market in Odesa region, an apartment building in Kharkiv region, Zelensky said.

A drone strike damaged a passenger train on the route between Kyiv and the eastern city of Sumy, though its 90 passengers and crew were able to evacuate beforehand, Ukraine’s emergency services said. While attacks on trains have become more frequent and passengers are often evacuated on their journeys, rail remains a popular way to travel between the cities.

Due to the scale of the Russian attack, military aircraft were put in the air by neighboring Poland to protect its airspace, the Reuters news agency reported, citing the country’s armed forces.

On Sunday, Witkoff and Kushner, US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, met with Ukrainian officials in Kyiv, one day after holding intensive meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow, as Washington renews its push to end the years-long war.

Residents stand at a site of a Russian missile and drone attack, amid Russia’s attack on Ukraine, in Kyiv, Ukraine, on September 8, 2026. Alina Smutko/Reuters

“Substantive progress was made, including movement on scheduling additional trilateral talks,” Witkoff said on X following the talks, though no major breakthroughs were announced.

Russia and Ukraine had agreed to pause attacks on each other’s capitals for the duration of the weekend of diplomacy, which came after months without significant progress toward resolution. The 72-hour truce expired on Tuesday.

The reprieve came after weeks of intense Russian attacks on the Ukrainian capital, including a daytime strike on the headquarters of Ukraine’s Security Service on Friday –– the first time the building had been hit during the conflict.

People take shelter inside a metro station during a Russian drone strike, amid Russia’s attack on Ukraine, in Kyiv, Ukraine September 8, 2026. Alina Smutko/Reuters

That strike was seen as a major escalation, and a sign that Kyiv is increasingly unable to defend its key assets against Russian attacks as it struggles with critical shortages of interceptor missiles.

Zelensky said Tuesday’s attack underscored that need.

“Despite very good results against cruise missiles, ballistic missiles remain particularly difficult to intercept, and every day we make the case to our partners for our need for interceptors,” he said.

Ukraine has ramped up its own aerial attacks in recent months, striking targets deeper into Russian territory.

A Ukrainian drone attack hit civilian infrastructure in the Russian city of Saratov, wounding ten people, including three children, the city’s governor said in a post to Telegram Tuesday.

This story has been updated with additional developments.

World.title: Military and intelligence officials discuss smaller presence in the Middle East as US looks for another post-9/11 strategy
World.content:
In offices across the military and in the intelligence community, there have been recent quiet discussions about cutting the number of people and facilities typically stationed in the Middle East if the Trump administration succeeds in ending the Iran conflict, six sources say.

If those cuts happen, it would mark another shift in how the US national security apparatus treats a region that successive presidents have sought to leave behind.

In the wake of the September 11, 2001, attacks, the US exponentially expanded a constellation of permanent military and intelligence facilities to fight wars and conduct strikes in half a dozen countries: Iraq, Afghanistan, Syria, Iran, Yemen, Libya.

But the recent fighting with Iran has laid bare deep vulnerabilities in the American infrastructure in the Middle East as many of those sites have become targets of repeated Iranian attacks in an unpopular war that has killed 18 American service members.

The remains of Army 1st Lt Tyler Feehan and Army Staff Sgt. Michael Emmanuel Swinton arrive at Dover Air Force Base on July 22 during a dignified transfer for military casualties of the war with Iran. Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images

Officials involved in the informal discussions in the military and the intelligence community indicated they are now acting at least in part to predict what might be acceptable to a mercurial president who sources say has articulated no clear strategy for a postwar future — and who, in the past, has staked his political identity on reducing American forces overseas.

Those discussions are happening even as there are still 50,000 troops and a large number of military assets in the Middle East, including two aircraft carriers and more than a dozen guided-missile destroyers. CIA officers who were sent home during the hottest part of the fighting earlier this year are being sent back to the region, one of the sources said.

The US military is also evaluating how to harden its defenses for those troops who are expected to remain in the region, even once the war ends. That includes by moving some installations underground to better defend against missile and drone attacks like those launched by Iran in the monthslong conflict, according to two sources familiar with the discussions.

While the Pentagon has long discussed moving some bases in the region underground, the idea took on new urgency after the first weeks of war as Iran exposed how vulnerable they were to drone and missile attacks.

“The vulnerabilities were always known, but the US never acted on it with urgency,” said one of the sources, a US official.

The military has developed several potential courses of action for changing the US force structure in the Middle East as soon as next year, two of the sources said — noting it would not make sense to abandon those strategic locations for launching aircraft while the conflict is ongoing.

The Office of the Secretary of Defense directed questions to US Central Command. Central Command did not respond to a query from CNN before publication. The Central Intelligence Agency declined to comment.

In the background of today’s discussion are the repeated planned pivots out of the region: 25 years of military intervention in the Middle East since September 11 with cycles of promises to pull back.

‘If we do’

The US military started dramatically increasing its footprint in the Middle East in the years before 9/11, maintaining a presence of roughly 27,000 active-duty troops across the region starting in 1998 — significantly more than in the decades prior.

That number would only continue to grow after the September 11 attacks, as US basing grew to support first the war in Afghanistan, then Iraq, then a metastasizing series of counterterrorism conflicts in hot spots around the region.

Two years after the September 11 attacks, the US had an estimated 250,000 troops in the Middle East during the invasion of Iraq. Between 2007 and 2011, the number of Americans in the region fluctuated but never dropped below roughly 100,000, according to publicly available estimates.

US Army soldiers take cover on March 27, 2003, near the town of An Najaf, Iraq. Scott Nelson/Getty Images

In 2011, then-President Barack Obama announced that “the tide of war is receding” in Afghanistan and that the US would begin drawing down tens of thousands of troops whom he had surged to the fight. The US would not withdraw fully from Afghanistan for another decade.

That same year, Obama withdrew combat troops from Iraq in a bid to extricate the US from a war widely seen as a failure. But he was forced to return when the vacuum of American power arguably led to the rise of ISIS.

Even as the total of US troops in the Middle East dropped in the years following 2011, it still hovered between 30,000 and 60,000. Throughout that time, the potential threat from Iran also loomed large in the mind of US policymakers, in particular proxy groups that launched fatal attacks on American service members in Iraq.

Though planners are discussing options for potential cuts now, the US appears no closer to negotiating a settlement with Iran that would end the conflict. Iran continues to target US bases and forces deployed to the region, launching attacks against American installations in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates last week as the two sides exchanged fire for the first time in roughly a month.

The damage has been substantial, US officials say: The CIA’s outpost in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, for example, was effectively destroyed by an Iranian attack, according to one US official and a former intelligence officer. Although Pentagon officials have sought to downplay the impact, American military installations in Bahrain, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Kuwait have all been struck by Iranian drones and missiles, and sources say the damage has been significant.

For the CIA and the military’s elite special operations command, some officials have considered whether the same sensitive jobs can be done without permanent basing, according to two US officials: leave personnel and equipment stationed in the United States, send them to the Middle East for individual missions, then return home.

In some cases, the US government may simply decline to rebuild assets that were severely damaged or destroyed by Iranian attacks — in part due to cost considerations, one official and two other sources familiar with the discussions said.

Pentagon officials have publicly refused to say what they might rebuild.

In April, Pentagon comptroller Jules “Jay” Hurst III told reporters it was not clear how much it would cost to repair bases and facilities damaged from the war with Iran, “and part of it is we would assess what our posture should be in the Middle East.”

Hurst later added that the Pentagon does not “have a final number for what the damage is to our installations overseas,” and it depends “on how we decide to rebuild those, or if we do.”

Senior Pentagon officials have privately made clear they want to scale back the US military’s troop presence in several Gulf countries as part of a broader effort to shift more of the defense burden onto regional partners, according to three sources familiar with the discussions.

US forces patrol oil fields near Syria’s northeastern border with Turkey in the Qahtaniyah countryside in the far northeast corner of Hasakeh province on September 3, 2024. Delil Souleiman/AFP/Getty Images

Sources said there was no official process or direct order to conduct what’s known formally as a force posture review. Officials within different parts of the military and the CIA are instead keenly aware that even as the military continues to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz, launch attacks on Iranian infrastructure and threaten strikes against additional targets that would likely further escalate the conflict, President Donald Trump is known to change his mind quickly.

“Is there an implicit task? Is there something coming down the pike where we need to be prepared to go, or are we sitting [forward] just in case?” said another US official, describing the tone of the discussions.

No clear timeline

The CIA was in search of a mission at the time of the 9/11 attacks, former officers and historians say: Its chief adversary, the Soviet Union, had fallen. There were analysts at the agency deeply steeped in terrorism and in the Middle East — but not many of them. Staff in the region probably numbered in the mere hundreds, according to Jeffrey Rogg, an intelligence historian at the University of Texas at Austin.

After 9/11, that all changed. The agency recruited heavily and grew a much larger cadre of paramilitary officers who carried guns and worked closely with the US military to hunt out terrorists — a contrast to the traditional picture of a case officer, who was tasked with developing source relationships and gathering secrets.

But both organizations lived through the ebbs and flows of a two-decade engagement in a region that presidents of both parties at times wanted desperately to leave behind. Obama sought to engineer a “pivot” of American military and intelligence resources to Asia; Trump’s administration in his first term ranked China as America’s biggest threat in his first national security strategy.

But the word “pivot” became a running joke in national security circles as successive crises and policy decisions — including the unforeseen rise of ISIS and Trump’s first-term decision to kill top Iranian Gen. Qasem Soleimani — continued to suck the United States back into the Middle East.

Top US military leaders have recently warned Trump that combat options for escalating the conflict with Iran are unlikely to achieve his stated objectives, CNN has reported, with the president instead opting to focus on ramping up economic pressure in hopes of crippling the regime.

But there is no clear timeline for how long that strategy may take to produce results, and many analysts believe that Iran’s current leadership may be willing to endure months of economic pain and is unlikely to capitulate in the near term.

Broadly, Pentagon officials expect to maintain some of the large, permanent military bases in the region, but rebuilding those installations may depend on the host nation’s willingness to contribute to the cost, which would likely be in the billions of dollars, one of the sources told CNN. The source added that many were originally constructed and paid for by the country in which they reside.

In the short term, US troops and bases in neighboring countries will almost certainly face continued attacks from Iran.

The Navy’s top admiral said last week that personnel would not be returning to Bahrain, the traditional home of the 5th Fleet, “anytime soon.”

“We’re not getting back in there anytime soon,” Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle said. “I just want to be completely honest with that.”

World.title: Egypt’s foreign currency reserve up to US$ 57.214 billion in August
World.content:
The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) announced that total international reserves rose to US$ 57.214 billion at the end of August 2026, compared to $ 56.293 billion at the end of the preceding month of July.

Foreign currency reserves increased by $921 million during August 2026, representing a monthly growth rate of 1.63 percent, to reach a total of $57.214 billion.

Banking expert Tarek Metwally said that the rise in Egypt’s foreign currency reserves reflects the continued improvement in foreign currency liquidity indicators and the Egyptian economy’s ability to meet its foreign currency needs.

Metwally added that the current increase in reserves is a positive indicator of the stability of the exchange market and the improvement in foreign currency sources, especially given the continued flow of remittances from Egyptians working abroad, the improvement in tourism revenues and foreign direct investment, in addition to the government’s efforts to increase exports and bolster its dollar reserves.

Reaching this level of reserves enhances the Central Bank’s ability to cope with any pressures or emergency needs related to foreign currency, he explained, and supports confidence in the Egyptian economy’s ability to meet its external obligations and pay its dues on time.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Iran announces imminent agreement with Oman on Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Iran announced on Monday that its negotiations with the Sultanate of Oman regarding the establishment of a safe and temporary shipping lane through the Strait of Hormuz have entered their final stages, anticipating an agreement in the coming days.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Ismail Baghaei said during his weekly press conference in Tehran that the talks saw “very good progress.”

He expressed hope that “third parties” would not interfere to obstruct the agreement.

The anticipated agreement aims to “organize a safe and temporary route for commercial vessels through the strait,” the spokesperson explained, noting the possibility of registering the agreement with the International Maritime Organization.

Data shows less ships transiting

Shipping data released on Monday showed that the daily average of commodity vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz was 10 over the past 10 days – the lowest level since May – following US and Iranian attacks on tankers.

Data from analytics platform Kpler indicated that the 10-day moving average was 10 vessels on Sunday, compared to more than 15 on Friday and around 13 on Saturday.

Only two ships transited the strait on Saturday, while six passed through on Sunday, most of them via the Iranian route.

The data further showed that a very large crude carrier (VLCC) and three bulk carriers loaded with minerals, grain, or oilseeds entered the strait on Sunday.

And data from the London Stock Exchange Group indicated that a tanker carrying refined petroleum products, loaded at a Saudi port, attempted to leave the strait but was forced to turn back.

The Kpler data also showed that no VLCCs have left the Strait of Hormuz since Wednesday.

World.title: When will old lease contracts expire? Everything you need to know
World.content:
As the expiration deadline for old lease contracts approaches for legal entities, interest amongst landlords and tenants alike has risen regarding when exactly these contracts will expire.

The Decisive Date

Old lease contracts are subject to the provisions of Law #10 of 2022, which regulates the rental relationship for legal entities, will expire in March 2027.

This law, ratified by the Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and published in the Official Gazette in March 2022, established a set of new regulations to govern the relationship between landlords and tenants in these contracts.

Five-Year Grace Period

The law grants “legal person” tenants a five-year transitional period, starting from its implementation date, with a 15 percent annual rent increase during this period.

At the end of the five years – specifically on March 2027 – existing leases subject to the law will expire, and the tenant will be obligated to return the leased property to its owner.

Who is subject to the law?

The term “legal persons” encompasses bodies and entities that own or lease properties under old lease agreements, including companies, associations, institutions, unions, ministries, and public authorities.

What Will Happen?

Upon the expiration of the legal grace period, the old lease agreement terminates, and the tenant is obligated to return the leased unit or property to the landlord.

However, if the tenant wishes to remain in the unit, both parties can agree on a new lease agreement, according to terms agreed upon between them.

The old contract therefore does not automatically continue after the grace period expires; rather, the continuation of the lease relationship is contingent upon the conclusion of a new contract between the parties.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: When is the trial operation for Egypt’s high-speed electric train?
World.content:
The head of the National Authority for Tunnels, Tarek Goweily, told the Extra News TV channel that trial operations for the high-speed electric train project will begin in October on the section from Ain Sokhna to 6th of October City.

He explained that the first line of the project, extending from Ain Sokhna to Marsa Matrouh, has reached completion rates between 85 percent and 88 percent.

The start of trial operations on the first section will be followed by gradual testing of the remaining sections of the line, Goweily added.

The implementation of the operational timeline depends on the completion of testing and obtaining international safety certification, he said, in addition to finalizing the training and qualification of the operating crews, including drivers and technicians

The German company responsible for operating the train began training the operating crews in February and is expected to complete this phase by February or March, thus preparing the crews to manage and operate the system.

The project’s impact extends beyond simply developing transportation, he said, explaining that the high-speed electric train will affect the urban and industrial communities along its route by contributing to the development of new areas and boosting investment and population growth along the line.

Goweily viewed the high-speed electric train project to be one of the most important pillars of modern transportation in Egypt, given its role in supporting the new urban and industrial areas along its route.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: This city is one of the world’s most important AI hubs. It’s not where you’d expect
World.content:
Toronto, Canada — Geoffrey Hinton, a Nobel Prize-winning computer scientist, took a leap in the 1980s — leaving a well-funded post at Carnegie Mellon University to pursue a little-studied area of machine learning research at the University of Toronto.

Four decades later, Hinton and that research paved the way for how modern AI systems function, all while changing the face of the Canadian city.

Silicon Valley is the beating heart of the tech industry, but a thriving AI ecosystem has developed around Hinton in Toronto.

Tech giants including Google, Nvidia, Meta and Microsoft, along with a slew of startups, have opened offices or research labs within miles of the University of Toronto. Even non-tech firms are now eyeing the city for its AI expertise: pharmaceutical company Sanofi this year announced a nearly $300 million investment in a Toronto AI Center of Excellence.

Toronto now boasts the world’s third best tech talent market, ahead of New York City but behind San Francisco and Seattle, according to an annual analysis by commercial real estate firm CBRE. That’s thanks to educational institutions like the University of Toronto, and public-private research institutes like the Vector Institute, which Hinton co-founded to help commercialize AI breakthroughs.

Cohere co-founder Nick Frosst, and Radical Ventures co-founder Jordan Jacobs and Geoffrey Hinton. CNN

“I was lucky because very few people were working on this 20 years ago, and so smart young students would come to Toronto … and they’ve now turned into a whole generation of AI leaders,” Hinton told CNN in an interview in Toronto.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is now aiming to boost the local AI ecosystem with a national AI strategy that includes more than $2 billion in spending on AI research, education and efforts to increase adoption, as well as new safety guardrails.

Toronto’s growing AI power comes as trade relations between the United States and Canada have deteriorated. A trade war has exploded in recent weeks, with Canadian officials seeking to protect the country’s industries. It may be yet another reason why the country’s tech investments are important.

“I don’t think we can afford for Canada to get all this technology from the States or from China,” Hinton said.

‘We liked it here’
